narrative_en: On a slope 2.2 m high within the workplace, a wire rope hooked onto the hook of the bucket of an excavator (backhoe) that was not of crane specification was wrapped around a felled zelkova tree, and when the boom was raised in order to carry the tree with the excavator, the excavator suddenly fell off the slope; the worker who was operating it was thrown from the operator's seat, was pinned under the excavator, and died.

The victim, who had returned to the workplace after finishing a taxi shift, got out of the company vehicle in order to swap it with a private car parked on the premises and approached the driver's seat of the private car; because the company vehicle was moving forward, the victim went around to its front to try to stop it, but could not stop it and was run over.

Three people, including the victims, were doing year-end cleaning; they spread thinner, a hazardous substance, on the floor and were scraping paint residue off the floor with scrapers when an explosion occurred, caused by sparks from the scrapers rubbing against the floor or by static electricity.

Three people, including the victims, were doing year-end cleaning; they spread thinner, a hazardous substance, on the floor and were scraping paint residue off the floor with scrapers when an explosion occurred, caused by sparks from the scrapers rubbing against the floor or by static electricity.

At a waste processing site, while performing work loading waste cardboard generated within the company into a packer truck (garbage truck), the victim's head was caught in the rotating plate of the packer truck. The plan for the work was that a coworker would hand the waste cardboard loaded on a roll box pallet to the victim, who would load it into the packer truck; when the coworker was about to make the first handover of cardboard, the coworker found the victim caught in the rotating plate.

Workers A, B and C began inspection and maintenance work on hoists and other equipment installed in the ceiling section of a multi-level parking structure with a total height of about 30 m. While worker B was ascending toward the ceiling on the carrier (which also had a passenger car on it) operated by worker C, the carrier suddenly fell at a height of 8 m. Worker A, who was working under the carrier, was pinned under the carrier and died.
While traveling on a national highway with one lane in each direction, the victim's vehicle crossed into the oncoming lane and collided head-on with an oncoming large truck.

At a clear-cutting site in the mountains, while the victim was sharpening a chainsaw in the middle of bucking work, a felled tree that had been placed on the upstream side of the valley slid down toward the downstream side and pierced the victim's abdomen.

While riding a moped on a road along a river to deliver morning newspapers, the victim fell into the river together with the motorcycle and died of a cervical spinal cord injury. The road being traveled had an asphalt surface and was about 3 meters wide. No guardrails or other fall-prevention measures were installed.

During expressway facility maintenance work to replace light bulbs in the upper part of a downbound tunnel, with the passing lane closed off, the work was completed, and in order to lift the lane closure the victim was placing three flares at 20 m intervals in the passing lane, starting from a point a further 100 m before the arrow board at the very front of the closure; while placing the third flare, the victim was run over by a car traveling straight along the passing lane.

At a road paving construction site, a public vehicle broke through a barricade on the road shoulder and entered the work area, struck the victim, who was patrolling the site, and collided with a parked excavator (backhoe). The victim was caught between the parked excavator and the vehicle and died.

Nurses and other staff working in the 2nd-floor nurses' room heard a thud like a package falling, went out of the nurses' room into the hallway, and found the victim lying spread-eagled on their back in the hallway directly below the stairs connecting the 2nd floor and the roof. An emergency call was made immediately and the nurses and other staff carried out lifesaving measures, but the victim died at the hospital to which they were transported.
On the road in front of the workplace, the victim was riding a bicycle when struck by a truck turning right.

The victim was operating an excavator (backhoe) at the accident site, feeding material onto a belt conveyor. Because the belt conveyor was malfunctioning, the victim, who is believed to have been inspecting the belt conveyor, had their head and hands caught in a pulley of the belt conveyor.

After road surface repair work on one lane of a road with two lanes in each direction was completed, during removal of the vehicle restriction zone, a security guard who was directing public traffic was run over by a 2 t truck reversing within the restriction zone.

While operating a vehicle-type construction machine (skid steer loader) to move it to a different parking location, the victim's body was caught between the machine's boom and the frame of the operator's seat.

The victim, who belonged to a primary subcontractor contracted for foundation work on a new building, was alone trying to load an excavator (backhoe) that had been used at the site onto a 3 t truck to take it back to the workplace; when lifting the front of the crawlers by bracing the bucket against the truck bed, the machine lost balance and overturned, and the victim, thrown from the operator's seat, had their chest caught by the head guard and died.

At a materials yard, three workers including the victim were putting away materials. Seventy-five plastic ground mats (weighing about 2.5 tons) were lifted with a single sling by an excavator (backhoe), and while the victim and one other worker were on the left and right sides of the lifted plastic mats, the mats collapsed and the victim fell backward. The victim struck their head on the ground in the fall and died.

The victim, an employee of a ready-mixed concrete manufacturing company, was found in cardiopulmonary arrest lying with blood coming from the head behind and to the left of a ready-mixed concrete truck on the company's premises, and died at the hospital to which they were transported.

To remove a foreign object that the business owner had mistakenly put into a cattle feed mixer, the victim, on the owner's instructions, entered the mixer and removed the foreign object. During this work, the owner left the site temporarily, returned a few minutes later, and started the mixer; the iron bar inside the mixer rotated and the victim was caught between the iron bar and the bottom of the mixer.

While pruning tall trees at a golf course, the victim was standing on a tripod stepladder and cutting branches with a chainsaw when they fell to the ground from a rung 1.59 meters above the ground, broke their neck, and died at the hospital to which they were transported.

An abnormality lamp was lit indicating that the carrier unit of a surface treatment (bonderizing) line had stopped; on checking, the victim was found with their chest caught between the carrier unit (a conveying device with a traveling motor) and a steel column of the treatment tank frame. The victim had been working alone replacing and repairing the water supply piping of the surface treatment (bonderizing) line.
The worker was found unconscious after falling from a stepladder (used extended like a ladder). The worker was transported to hospital and remained unconscious, but died.

While returning to a fishing port after fishing, the fishing boat the victim was aboard capsized and was lost; the victim was later found drifting in the surrounding waters, was transported to a medical facility, and death was then confirmed.

While paving work was being performed with part of the upbound lane of a motorway closed off, a light vehicle (kei car) traveling in the downbound lane crossed the restriction and entered, striking two workers and one security guard working within the restricted area; the security guard died at the hospital to which they were transported.

The victim, who had gone down from the water receiving tank room on basement level 1 to basement level 2 to work on adjusting the residual chlorine concentration of a pool, was found lying bleeding beside the fixed ladder connecting basement levels 1 and 2. The victim was hospitalized and received treatment, but died.
A 1 t load fell from a forklift during unloading of a truck, and a worker working nearby was pinned underneath and died.
While traveling on a national highway, the victim collided with a soundproof wall between the side road and the main road.

In the soil calcination process at a contaminated soil treatment facility, two workers were raking out calcined soil on the external belt conveyor near the calcined soil discharge outlet at the bottom of the plant equipment when calcined soil that had fallen inside the silo was released from the outlet; the two workers were exposed to its heat and suffered full-body burns. The victims were transported by ambulance and were undergoing treatment at a medical facility when they died as a result of the full-body burns.

In the soil calcination process at a contaminated soil treatment facility, two workers were raking out calcined soil on the external belt conveyor near the calcined soil discharge outlet at the bottom of the plant equipment when calcined soil that had fallen inside the silo was released from the outlet; the two workers were exposed to its heat and suffered full-body burns. The victims were transported by ambulance and were undergoing treatment at a medical facility when they died as a result of the full-body burns.

On the platform (about 1 m high) of a warehouse on the workplace premises, after operating a forklift to move loads, the victim reversed, fell off the platform together with the forklift, was thrown from the operator's seat, was pinned under the frame of the forklift's head guard, and died.

At a steel product storage area, the victim and two coworkers had placed a steel member (about 6 meters long, weighing about 1 ton) spanning across stands with square timbers in between, and while scraping the steel member, it fell together with the timbers from a height of about 66 centimeters above the ground toward the victim's side, struck the victim's back, and crushed the upper body, and the victim died.
While driving through a tunnel on the upbound lane of an expressway, the victim rear-ended a trailer that had stopped due to traffic congestion.

At a clear-cutting site in a town-owned forest, while moving on foot along a work road, the victim was struck by a tree felled with a chainsaw by a coworker lower down the slope. The tree that struck the victim had a diameter at breast height of 32 cm and a height of 29.6 m.
While the victim was traveling south on an expressway in a light truck, an oncoming vehicle (a light truck) traveling north entered the victim's lane, resulting in a head-on collision.

At a hotel renovation site, while two workers were carrying restaurant fixtures up the stairs installed outside the restaurant to bring them from a truck into the 1st-floor restaurant, one worker lost their balance, slipped through a gap in the stair handrail, and fell about 4 m to the middle of the adjacent stairs leading to the basement fire-extinguishing equipment room; death was confirmed the same day.

At an onion sorting facility, the onion feeding device called the "damper" came into contact with the forks of a forklift and was broken, and the victim and a coworker were repairing it; the chain cover was acting as a stopper holding the damper in place, but the victim did not notice this, and when the victim removed the chain cover the damper's frame rotated, catching the victim's upper body, and the victim died.

The victim was driving a van to transport two facility users and was traveling on a municipal road leading to a residential area; going down a slope and attempting to turn at a T-junction onto a prefectural road, the vehicle could not stop and collided head-on with a wall at the roadside.

Two trucks and other vehicles were parked in the right lane of a national highway with two lanes in each direction, with traffic cones, signs and other items placed in front of them, and work such as mowing grass on the median strip was being performed when a 4-ton truck traveling in that lane struck one traffic controller and one worker; both were transported to a medical facility but died the same day.

Two trucks and other vehicles were parked in the right lane of a national highway with two lanes in each direction, with traffic cones, signs and other items placed in front of them, and work such as mowing grass on the median strip was being performed when a 4-ton truck traveling in that lane struck one traffic controller and one worker; both were transported to a medical facility but died the same day.

At a residential land development site, during excavation work using two backhoes, the ground under the backhoe positioned on the upper level collapsed, and it fell and crashed into the backhoe positioned on the lower level. At that time, it crushed the worker in the operator's seat of the lower backhoe.

At a delivery destination, the victim was alone attempting to unload a cable drum (a drum wound with electric cable, weighing about 1 t) from the bed of a truck-mounted crane; the cable drum fell from the truck bed or the crane hook, and the victim was found pinned underneath it.

On the day of the accident, the victim and coworkers had entered the tracks within a station and were preparing for rail welding work; while crossing the downbound line to carry equipment that had been temporarily placed there, the victim was struck by an approaching freight train.
While engaged in defrosting and cleaning work inside a freezer, the victim was found caught in the freezer entrance door (123 cm wide, 206 cm high).

The victim, who had been pruning an oak hedge, was found lying on the dirt ground with a head injury. From the circumstances at the time of discovery, it is presumed that the victim fell while pruning on a stepladder with a pruning tool called a trimmer.

As the victim was going straight through an intersection from east to west, a passenger car going straight from south to north crashed into the area between the truck's left fuel tank and rear wheels; the impact flipped the truck and it overturned onto the driver's side. The driver's side had overturned onto the guardrail, and the cab was deformed.
The victim was felling trees in a windbreak forest on a golf course with a chainsaw and was found unconscious, leaning against the tree next to the tree being felled.

The victim's coworker arrived at the accident site and, as the cargo vehicle the victim had been driving was parked there, approached it and found the victim in a sitting position facing the truck bed, pinned under two roll box pallets loaded with cargo on a platform 30 cm above ground level at the warehouse loading entrance. The victim was transported to hospital, but death from traumatic asphyxia was confirmed.

During unloading work using an excavator (backhoe), the operator, without switching the excavator (a machine with mobile crane specification, with a rated lifting load of 0.9 t in crane mode) to crane mode, operated it to lift earth-retaining materials (weighing 1.2 t) from a truck bed and swung it, whereupon the excavator toppled over and the head of the victim, who was steadying the load by hand, was caught between the arm and the ground.

The front wheels of a forklift driven by a coworker dropped into the gap between the platform and a truck and became stuck. The victim operated another forklift to try to lift the stuck forklift but could not lift it, and when reversing made an operating error and fell together with the forklift from the platform, which was about 1 m high, was pinned under the forklift, and died. The victim was wearing a safety helmet.

At a stockyard for crushed stone, a raw material of ready-mixed concrete, the victim was found buried in crushed stone. The victim was the driver of the dump truck that had transported the crushed stone.
At the company's materials yard, while the victim was guiding a truck, the victim was run over by an excavator (backhoe) operated by an employee as it reversed, and died.

While two security guards, victim A and victim B, were opening a gate, a trailer collided with the gate. Victim B, who was near the gate, was thrown by the impact and collided with victim A, and victim A died of a skull fracture, cerebral contusion and other injuries.
While working on a roof about 6.8 meters high to paint the roof of a private house, the victim fell from the roof for some reason and died.

An employee found the victim, who belonged to a waste paper collection business, with their legs caught in the compression plate of the mechanical operating section at the rear loading opening of a waste paper collection packer truck, unable to move and calling for help; when the employee, attempting a rescue, operated the controls as the victim explained, the compression plate of the mechanical operating section drew the victim into the back of the vehicle's loading compartment up to the chest.

To check the firing status, the victim checked the kiln alone and sensed an abnormality in the kiln. The victim telephoned the person in charge to come to the kiln and pressed the kiln's ignition button, whereupon LP gas that had filled the kiln ignited and exploded.

To return to the company from a construction site, the victim was riding in the front passenger seat of a van on a national highway with one lane in each direction. The van collided head-on with a pickup truck coming from the opposite direction, both vehicles went off the road, and the victim died. The weather was a snowstorm and the road surface was compacted snow.

After marking bucking positions on felled trees as an assistant in log processing with a grapple saw, the victim moved aside next to the grapple saw to keep clear, and was struck by a standing tree (about 22 m tall, about 30 cm in diameter at breast height) on which the victim had been doing felling work in the morning.

While driving a truck on a national highway from the workplace to make a delivery, the victim veered into the opposite lane and collided head-on with a large truck traveling in the oncoming lane. The victim died.

The victim was stringing wire cable for suspending telephone lines in the mountains. After the morning's work ended, while descending the mountain for a break, the victim fell and struck their chest hard. The victim took leave from work and was resting at home, where the victim was found collapsed.

To transport thatch grass growing in a company-owned rice paddy, the victim was driving a tractor shovel (machine weight 2.125 tons) along a raised path between paddies leading to the paddy; after traveling about 65 meters along the path, the shovel fell from the path shoulder on the right side of the direction of travel into the paddy 50 centimeters below, and the victim was thrown from the operator's seat. The victim was pinned under the post-type head guard of the fallen shovel, with the chest compressed, and suffocated.

At a demolition site, when a flexible container bag of waste materials was about to be moved with a demolition grapple, the victim, who was hooking the bag onto the grapple's claws, signaled to close the claws; the operator closed the claws within a safe range and checked with the victim by horn that it was safe, received a signal that all was well, and closed the claws further, whereupon the victim suddenly dropped to their knees and sat down. The victim was bleeding from the ears and nose, was unconscious, and died of multiple skull fractures.

The victim was pruning a Japanese yew tree about 4.9 meters tall when they fell to the ground from the 3.0-meter-high tripod stepladder being used for the work, struck their head, suffered a serious cervical spinal cord injury, and died of hypoxic encephalopathy.

During work including felling dead trees at a golf course, the victim was engaged in carrying branches after the delimbing of a felled tree. The felled tree was lying diagonally on a slope face, and while the victim was positioned below the felled tree to collect branches, the felled tree began to roll and struck the victim.

The victim loaded a total of 30 roll box pallets (about 3 t) onto an 11.7 t van-type truck and, while transporting them to the shipper, stopped on the road shoulder (uphill gradient of about 8 degrees) a few hundred meters before the shipper's premises. A few minutes later, a passing driver found the victim pinned under 10 roll box pallets (about 1 t) on the road a few meters behind the truck's rear doors. There were no scratches on the inside of the rear doors, and the lashing belt securing the pallets had come off its ratchet tensioner.
While driving a large truck on an expressway, the victim rear-ended a large truck that had had a tire burst and was stopped in the travel lane.

The victim was coupling a trailer to the truck (tractor unit) in the workplace parking lot and got out of the truck without applying the truck's parking brake. When the trailer and truck were coupled, the trailer's brakes were released. The victim, trying to stop the trailer as it started to move, was run over by the vehicle, and later died at the hospital to which they were transported.
While carrying a passenger in a taxi, the victim got into a dispute with the passenger and was struck on the head by the passenger, then lost consciousness and died.

The accident site was the demolition site of a storage shed built on the grounds of a private house. While the victim was demolishing wall materials from inside the shed using a crowbar, the shed's roof fell and the victim was pinned under the roof.
While driving on an expressway as part of their duties as a motor vehicle driver, the victim collided with the right-side guard cable of the expressway.

At a wastewater treatment facility, while the victim and two others were cleaning a flow equalization tank, the victim fell into the tank through an opening (600 mm x 1,700 mm) at the top of the tank (height about 6 m). The victim was transported to hospital but died the same day.

A worker engaged in felling obstructing trees for overhead line installation was dealing with a hung-up tree. Just before, the worker had delimbed a felled tree, and then, while making the face notch on the first of the two trees in which the tree was hung up, a branch that had been cut off slid down the slope and struck the victim, leaving the victim crouched at the bottom of the slope. At that moment, the supporting tree in which the face notch had been made broke, and the hung-up tree struck the victim's back. The victim's neck was compressed by their clothing, resulting in an intracranial hematoma, and the victim died at the hospital to which they were transported.

In preparation for temporarily placing renovation roofing members (metal) on the slate roof of a factory building, the victim climbed onto the slate roof and was setting timber sleepers on which to place the members. At that time, the victim stepped through the plastic skylight section of the slate roof and fell from a height of about 4.7 m onto the concrete floor of the factory.

It is believed that the victim fell from around the 2nd floor to the 1st floor of the permanent staircase (with handrails) inside the building (two stories) concerned. The 2nd-floor opening at the top of the permanent staircase had a wooden cover (with stops to prevent shifting), and when the victim was found it had come off.

In layer B of No. 2 hold inside a refrigerated cargo ship under construction, near an opening temporarily created by opening a hatch to bring in materials, while a two-person team including the victim was adjusting the position of floor materials, the victim lost balance, fell through the opening 6,800 millimeters down to layer D, and died.

At a workplace handling metal scrap, while metal scrap was being handled with an excavator (backhoe) fitted with a lifting magnet as an attachment (equivalent to a mobile crane), the victim, who had entered the swing radius, was struck by the load or other objects as the excavator swung and suffered a head injury.

In connection with removing corrugated sheets installed on the roof of a factory building, the victim climbed the steel pipe uprights of the scatter-prevention sheeting to check how the corrugated sheets were installed. When the victim stepped onto the slate of the eaves, using it as a foothold to move from the steel pipe uprights of the scatter-prevention sheeting to the factory building, the slate broke and the victim fell about 4.5 m to the ground.

A worker removing temporary electric cables run into a land development construction site was using a stepladder and, when cutting a temporary cable above the distribution panel (about 300 cm above ground), lost balance, fell into an irrigation channel, and died. The cutting work required stepping on the 4th step of the stepladder; that rung was 112 cm above ground, and the height from the 4th rung to the bottom of the irrigation channel was about 390 cm.

At the warehouse where cargo was being loaded, the victim was standing on rice bags stacked on a pallet on the truck bed and manually loading rice bags brought by forklift. When the forklift operator reversed the forklift at the victim's signal, the victim fell from the rice bags on the truck bed to the ground and struck their head hard. The victim was hospitalized and treated, but died.

After collecting eggs at chicken houses located around the workplace premises, the victim was heading in a light truck to the egg-washing area to wash the collected eggs; while trying to go up a slope from a chicken house, the vehicle driven by the victim rolled backward, fell to the bottom of the slope, and overturned. The victim went into cardiopulmonary arrest and was transported to hospital, and death was confirmed the same day.

In a freezer inside a refrigerated warehouse, the victim, who had been doing shipping work for frozen food products, was found collapsed between a shelf (about 2.1 meters high) holding frozen food products and a forklift, was transported to a medical facility, and died of severe head trauma.

At a warehouse roof painting site, the victim was working with the business owner on painting the roof and walls, and the business owner found the victim lying on the ground. The victim was transported to hospital but died of traumatic shock.

While a 151 cm wide belt conveyor carrying crushed material was running, the victim tried to remove with the right hand a foreign object stuck in the lower part of the belt conveyor; the right hand was caught in the pulley, the victim was drawn in up to the right half of the body, and died.

The victim was riding a carrier dump (crawler carrier) to transport soil and was traveling from the loading location to the unloading location when, for some reason, the carrier dump turned sharply to the left and ran off the haul road. The carrier dump broke through the single-pipe handrail on the road shoulder and fell, with the victim, from a retaining wall under construction about 12 meters high, crashing into the ground. After the accident the carrier dump was found upside down, and the victim's death was confirmed at the scene.

While an event was being set up at an event hall, a person working nearby heard a loud noise, looked in the direction of the sound, and found the victim lying on their back. When found, the victim did not respond when called, but breathing was confirmed. The victim was transported by ambulance the same day, but died at a later date.

The victim entered the site together with two employees for clear-cutting of forest owned by the workplace and was loading bark at the log landing using a vehicle-type construction machine, but did not return even after the end of working hours, and was found lying with blood coming from the head near where a hung-up tree, created when an employee was felling with a feller buncher, had fallen.

Having finished duties at the construction site that was the day's security post, the victim was riding in the front passenger seat of a company car (passenger car) driven by a coworker who had also been providing security at the same site, to return to the company, when the company car collided with a traffic signal pole at an intersection on the route back.

While the victim was adjusting the height of the grinding wheel of the grinder section of a grinding machine (a dedicated machine for deburring machined gears), the rotating grinding wheel (100 mm in diameter, 2 mm thick) broke and a fragment of the wheel struck the victim's face. The victim died the same day of hemorrhagic shock.

In the molding process for recycled crushed stone (the process of compacting ash, cement and other materials into blocks), a worker engaged in operating the ash solidification block production equipment was found with their abdomen caught between the frame of the chain conveyor sending products from the molding process to the curing process (the process that advances the solidification reaction of the cement) and a pallet carrying molded blocks, and death was later confirmed.

While the victim was clear-cutting with a chainsaw in a forest together with a coworker, after felling a Japanese cedar growing on a slope with a 20-degree incline, as the victim tried to move away from the felled tree, a dead Japanese cypress (hinoki) that had been entangled with the felled tree by wisteria vines fell and struck the victim; the victim's abdomen was caught between the slope and the dead tree, and the victim died.

The victim was driving a forwarder loaded with felled timber, traveling down a forest road in reverse; on reaching a curve in the forest road, the right rear part of the machine as seen from the operator's seat rode up onto an earth mound and a root stump at the side of the road, and the momentum caused the forwarder to overturn to the left as seen from the operator's seat. At that time, the victim was thrown from the operator's seat to the ground, and the area around the back of the victim's head was caught between the overturned forwarder and the ground.

The victim, a truck driver, fell (or tripped) while getting out of the truck's driver's seat on the shipper's premises and injured their head and buttocks. The victim continued working, returned to the workplace, and reported the injury. The victim worked normally the next day, but from the day after that, with scheduled days off in between, the victim could not be contacted, and was found dead at home. (Cause of death: "epidural hematoma, traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage")

While traveling in a company car from the sales office to a client, proceeding northeast after a large curve on a prefectural road, around the end of the curve the car crossed the oncoming lane and crashed into a retaining wall at the roadside. The victim was transported by ambulance but subsequently died.

During sewer construction work, one worker (the victim), accompanied by one security guard, was doing marking work on the road. Near the end of the work, the victim instructed the security guard, who had been directing traffic on the road, to work at another location. Afterward, the victim was struck by a taxi, was transported to hospital, and death was confirmed.

To prune a tree, the victim leaned a portable ladder against a utility pole and climbed to a height of about 2.5 m, then lost balance and fell. The victim was climbing the ladder to prepare before the pruning work and was not holding any tools.

At a used car dealership, after measuring the interior dimensions of the cargo bed of a cargo vehicle for sale (van / rear opening / maximum load capacity 13.3 t / no tailgate lift / bed height 1.1 m), the victim fell backward while climbing down from the rear of the cargo bed using the step and suffered a head injury. The victim died after being transported by ambulance.

At an expressway paving construction site, the victim, who was laying turf on the slope shoulder of a ramp (a road connecting the expressway and ordinary roads), was run over near the center of the road by a truck (flatbed, maximum load capacity 2.3 t) that was reversing with turf loaded on its bed.
While loading palletized cargo with a hand pallet truck, the cargo on a pallet collapsed inside the bed of a large truck and fell onto the victim's head.

At an exterior wall renovation site of a five-story hospital, while the victim was repairing holes in the exterior wall from which wall ties had been removed, in parallel with scaffold dismantling being carried out by a scaffolding contractor, the victim fell to the ground.

A truck transporting machine parts rear-ended a truck that had stopped in the passing lane after a tire burst and engine stall, and the driver of the rear-ending truck died. The truck had been traveling for an hour and a half since departure, and its last recorded speed was 92 kilometers per hour. It reportedly crashed into the other truck without braking. After the accident, the rear-ending truck was carried by the momentum to the road shoulder and stopped.

The victim stopped a passenger car on a sloping road and got out, but because the parking brake had not been applied, the car rolled backward; the victim noticed and hurriedly tried to stop the car but could not, and fell together with the car into a 2.3-meter-deep waterway beside the road.

During crack repair work on a cyclone of the preheater equipment, the victim began grinding rust on the work platform beside the cyclone; after 30 minutes, the person in charge called to the victim, "Let's take a break," and left the work area first, but as the victim did not follow, the person in charge returned to the work area and found the victim collapsed; together with coworkers, they brought the victim down from the equipment, gave first aid such as cooling the neck, and transported the victim to hospital by ambulance, but the victim died.

A security guard patrolling inside a hospital fell from an existing winding staircase in the hospital building. Security camera footage confirmed that the victim entered the winding staircase from the 6th floor, and about 4 minutes later there was a loud impact sound, and the victim was found bleeding at the lowest level of the winding staircase, basement level 1.

On the roof of a three-story factory, the victim was working alone putting rain covers over flexible container bags (weighing about 500 kg) containing powdered polyvinyl alcohol, a material for the product. When the victim used a crane to place a new flexible container bag on top of an existing one and tried to put the rain cover over it, the bag fell toward the victim, and the victim's body was caught between the bag and a brace reinforcing the crane's base frame, and the victim died.

The victim, the driver of a cargo vehicle (load capacity 12.8 tons) transporting logs, was waiting to unload at a timber yard in a port and was greasing on the right side of the truck bed when the hook of a chain securing the logs came off, the logs collapsed, and they struck the victim's head. There was no damage to the chain, but the pin to keep the hook from coming off had not been inserted. Also, because the truck was waiting to unload, the stanchions for preventing falls had been removed from the truck bed.

While the victim was cutting a U-shaped flume (made of concrete) placed on the ground using an engine cutter (power cutter), the blade of the engine cutter contacted the left side of the victim's neck, and the victim died of blood loss from the laceration.

A 2-ton truck driven by one of the victims was traveling on a national highway to a security site when, passing through a tunnel, it collided for some reason with a retaining wall located to the north (single-vehicle accident). The front of the 2-ton truck was severely deformed. The two workers in the driver's seat and the front passenger seat were injured, and the passenger died.

During work to lay electrical cables in underground conduits, while the cables were being pulled in using an electric winch and wire rope, the mounting bracket of the pulley through which the wire rope ran came off the concrete box structure, sprang up, and struck the victim's upper body.

After loading of a container-type truck was completed at the shipping area, the rear doors could not be closed because they were warped, so the driver and the victim discussed it and decided to reverse the truck into the building to correct the warp. When the driver reversed the truck into the building and then drove it forward to check the warp in the doors, the victim was found lying on the ground.

At a sawmill, while timber (3 m long, 30 cm wide, 8 cm thick, weighing about 50 kg) was being conveyed on a roller conveyor, two pieces of timber became jammed where the conveyor narrowed; after the conveyor was stopped, the victim moved onto a wooden board laid between the rollers and, when lifting one of the jammed pieces of timber to move it, fell backward, falling with the timber 1.8 m from the wooden board onto the concrete floor, and the falling timber struck the victim's chest.

While the victim was riding a moped northeast on a national highway to deliver newspapers, the victim was struck by a vehicle from behind at an intersection, suffered impacts to the whole body, and died. Brake marks from the following vehicle were left before the pedestrian crossing at the intersection in the northeast-bound direction of the national highway.

The victim was laying sandbags (about 5 kg) under solar panels on sloped land (1:3 gradient) when instructed to move a hand-guided rough terrain carrier; while, for some reason, moving again the carrier that a coworker had moved from the bottom to the top of the slope, the victim was caught between the carrier the victim was operating and a support post of a solar panel.

At a construction site, while workers (five, including the victim) were loading steel scaffold materials onto the bed of a cargo vehicle, the cargo vehicle, which was parked on a slope, ran away down the slope and, with the victim still on its bed, went over the site's slope face and fell to the ground more than 4 m below. The victim was thrown from the bed and hit the ground first, was struck immediately afterward by the falling vehicle body, and died.

Having become aware of an equipment malfunction, the victim was dealing with it on a work platform (about 4.5 m above the 1st-floor floor) installed at the 2nd-floor level of an open atrium area; after finishing, for some reason the victim fell from the work platform, the victim's legs struck a cart on the 1st floor, flipping the body over, and the victim's head struck the floor hard. After the accident, death was confirmed at the hospital where the victim had been admitted.

At a leased warehouse, four workers were receiving flexible container bags of rice delivered by truck (weighing the bags and temporarily placing them at designated locations in the warehouse). The bags were carried by forklift; after the operator placed a bag at the designated location and was reversing while turning the steering wheel for the next task, the operator felt the forklift ride over something, checked the surroundings, and found the victim lying on the ground.

In the ball mill room, the victim was washing hard balls using a mixer (ball mill: drum diameter 550 mm to 580 mm). As the victim could not be found at the lunch break, a coworker checked the ball mill room and found the victim caught in the mixer. The victim was transported to a medical facility, but death was later confirmed.

To remove the attachment of a vehicle-type construction machine (pile driver) scheduled to be used at the next site, the victim climbed onto the machine body and was removing bolts when the victim lost balance, fell from a height of 1.9 m to the ground, and died.

During log extraction from clear-cutting on a slope (about 35 degrees), when a coworker felled a Japanese cedar (about 22 meters tall), the impact of the fall broke off the top section with branches and leaves (about 6 meters). The trunk section of the felled tree (about 16 meters) slid down the slope and crashed into the grapple of the victim, who was removing fallen trees on the forest road. The felled tree went through the front right side window of the grapple and struck the victim's abdomen directly.

While driving a trailer north on a national highway, when passing through an intersection, the trailer's right front wheel rode up onto a median block, and the momentum caused the left front of the tractor unit (trailer head) to collide with the guardrail on the sidewalk side. The victim was not wearing a seatbelt and was thrown out of the vehicle in the collision.

At a building demolition site, during demolition of a concrete block wall (about 57 m long), when the end of the block wall was pulled down with the working device of a vehicle-type construction machine, the entire (upper part of the) block wall fell over, and the victim, who was about 43 m from the machine, was pinned underneath. The victim had been removing cables and other items fixed to the concrete base wall supporting the lower part of the block wall.

One subcontractor worker was pinned under a block wall that fell over and died the same day. In demolishing an L-shaped block wall about 2 meters high, part of the first course of blocks was cut with a cutter, and while the remaining part was being cut, with two workers holding the wall up so that it would not fall, in order to demolish only part of it, the block wall collapsed and the victim was pinned underneath.

The victim was working alone felling trees at a tree felling and extraction site when a tree being felled fell in a direction different from the face notch and struck the victim's back. There were no witnesses to the accident; a worker at the same site found the victim crouched over at a time believed to be immediately after the accident. The victim was transported by ambulance and treatment continued, but the victim died.

The victim was moving to the downbound platform of a station to go on a business trip. The victim ducked under the barrier of the level crossing on the west side within the station premises and was struck by a passing limited express train.

The victim was applying waterproof sheeting on the roof of a stairwell structure on the roof of a multi-tenant building when, for some reason, the victim fell from the edge and dropped about 15 m to the ground.
At the shipper's workplace, the victim was found beside a truck with a sheet lying over their body.

During compaction work with a plate compactor, water needed to be supplied, and it was decided to supply it from the water tank of a tire roller (maximum load capacity 3.5 t); behind the tire roller, the victim prepared a plastic water container and signaled the tire roller operator to start the pump, and when the operator revved the engine to raise the water supply pressure, the tire roller moved backward and ran over the victim.

During dismantling work on a boarding bridge (passenger boarding bridge), the victim was attempting to remove an inflated tire. After removing the fixing bolts of the wheel (split rim), the victim struck the hub nut that fixes the wheel to the axle using a chisel and hammer, whereupon the tube inside the tire expanded and burst, blowing off the tire and wheel. The victim was blown away at the same time and was found lying at a location about 14 m from the work position.

At a land development construction site, during work loading soil generated by ground excavation into a dump truck with an excavator (backhoe), the dump truck was reversing toward the excavator to be loaded, and the victim's head was caught between the excavator bucket and the dump truck. The victim died of multiple injuries.

While driving a large truck delivering frozen food, the victim collided with the wall at a tunnel entrance and sustained a head injury, and death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

While pulling and moving a roll box pallet loaded with garbage alone, the victim fell from the edge of a platform to the ground about 1.15 m below and fractured the cervical spine. The victim was hospitalized and received treatment, but died.

During demolition work on a store building (8 stories above ground, steel and reinforced concrete construction), a worker operating a vehicle-type construction machine (for demolition) was found unconscious, seated in the operator's seat of the machine, at a stairway between the 4th and 5th floors inside the store. The worker was taken to hospital but subsequently died.

During pruning of a pine tree about 5.6 m tall, the victim, who was working after climbing to the 5th or 6th step of a tripod stepladder, lost balance and fell to the ground. The height of the 6th step of the tripod stepladder was 164 cm.

A victim engaged in tree felling and related work in a national forest did not return after the end of working hours, so the work area was searched and the victim was found pinned under a fallen dead tree. At the site there was a stump from a felled tree, and vines were wrapped around the dead tree, which had fallen from its roots. When found, the dead tree lay over the victim's back, and the victim was in a sitting-like posture with both knees bent and the upper body face down.

A co-worker found the victim in a hanging state, with the hood of the rain jacket the victim was wearing caught in the shaft of an automatic opening/closing device of a plastic greenhouse owned by the establishment. A ladder was leaning against the greenhouse next to where the victim was hanged.

The victim, who was in charge of installing retaining wall blocks against natural ground, was installing a retaining wall with two co-workers when a support holding a retaining wall block (1 × 1 m, weighing about 540 kg) came off. Because the block was standing on its own, the victim entered the space between the natural ground and the block to pick up the detached support, whereupon the block fell over, and the victim was caught between the natural ground and the block and died.
A taxi driven by the victim, traveling on a prefectural road with one lane in each direction, crossed the center line and collided head-on with a wagon traveling in the oncoming lane.

While the victim was shaping a slope at an excavation site using an excavator (backhoe) (machine weight 26.5 tonnes, bucket capacity 1.4 m3), the victim fell together with the excavator into a sump (a pit for collecting rainwater etc., about 13 m square and about 4 m deep) located immediately next to the work area, and drowned in the sump. At the time of the accident, the sump was full of water due to rainfall and other factors.

On a public road at a construction site for a new 6-story reinforced concrete apartment building, the victim, who was performing traffic guidance, was crouching in front of a concrete mixer truck when the truck started moving and ran over the victim, who died.

During publicly funded demolition of a 2-story wooden detached house, the victim climbed onto the platform between the back of the cab and the cargo bed of a truck with a maximum load capacity of 3.8 tonnes to take a tool from a toolbox placed there, slipped, and fell onto the truck's cargo bed (1.5 m). The victim struck the left side of the head hard on an ornamental ridge-end tile (onigawara) loaded on the bed and was in critical condition, unconscious, and died of brain contusion. (At the time of the accident, the victim was wearing a safety helmet for fall protection.)

To dismantle a scaffold erected around the outside of a factory building, the victim, on the roof of the building, held a scaffold standard (upright) member to remove it, whereupon the victim's right upper arm contacted a point where the insulation of the service drop line to the building (live, 100 V) had peeled off and the conductor was exposed, and the victim was electrocuted.

On the ground, using two steel beams as sleepers, the victim and two others were attaching members to a steel beam (weighing about 2.5 t) resting on them. The victim was in charge of temporary bolting, attaching vertical nets, and slinging. While the victim was attaching a vertical net, the steel beam fell off the steel members used as sleepers and struck the victim.

In a double-bottom tank located below the engine room of a ship being outfitted, the victim had been spray painting with Class 2 organic solvents (paint). After finishing painting and exiting the tank, sparks falling from above in the engine room ignited organic vapor that had accumulated in the tank, causing an explosion. The victim was blown away by the blast and died of cervical spine injury.

The victim opened the double doors of the container on a hook-lift (arm-roll) truck loaded with plastic ground boards, banner flag poles, etc., took out banner flag poles, handed them to a co-worker, and approached the container doors again, whereupon the plastic ground boards collapsed and the victim was pinned under them.

The victim and co-workers, four people in total, were cutting bamboo and grass beside a municipal road. The victim was carrying cut bamboo in the bamboo grove along the road, and co-worker A was cutting the felled bamboo into short lengths with a brush cutter. While carrying cut bamboo past a point about 2 m behind co-worker A, the victim for some reason staggered and fell, contacted the blade of the co-worker's brush cutter, and suffered a cut to the neck.

The victim was performing parking work (driving used cars brought by tow truck and parking them in designated positions) in a motor pool where used cars for export were lined up and stored. After parking an incoming car in its designated position and getting out of it, the victim was scanning a management IC chip near the passenger door when struck by a vehicle driven by a co-worker, and died.

At a road construction site on a prefectural road, the victim was directing traffic for alternating one-way traffic and signaled a general vehicle traveling in the stopping direction to stop, but the vehicle did not stop and ran over the victim. The victim remained unconscious after the accident and subsequently died.
While working inside manufacturing equipment to dismantle it, a clasp suddenly came loose, and the top plate fell and struck the victim.

The victim and temple visitors were traveling in a vehicle owned by the establishment along the road between the temple parking lot and the temple when the vehicle fell (went over the edge). The road at the point of the fall was narrow and had a curve.

Victim A was operating a forklift to stack flexible container bags containing brown rice, and victim B was guiding the forklift, when previously stacked bags collapsed and victim B was pinned under them. Victim A called victim C and co-worker D for a rescue, and while they were approaching victim B, the bags collapsed further, and victims A and C were pinned under them. Victim A died as a result of this accident.
During pruning of garden trees, the victim fell from a stepladder (tripod type) and struck the head hard.

In a warehouse at an unloading destination, the victim was transporting 30 plywood sheets for fittings (total weight about 150 kg) on a roll box pallet when, for some reason, the victim fell over together with the load and struck the head on the concrete floor.

At the lower part of a conveyor called the "secondary crusher" in a wood resource recycling plant, the victim was cleaning by stretching the body with a jig to remove foreign matter adhering to the roller section through which the belt passes, was caught in the roller section, and died.

While the victim, at the upper part of a mountain slope, was hauling felled trees using a swing yarder by remote control, the tip of a tree being hauled caught on the ground, causing the butt end of the tree to lift up and strike the victim's chest.

The victim was covering materials with cardboard at a materials yard to keep them from getting wet in the rain. While carrying a flat concrete slab to place on the cardboard to hold it down, the victim fell and injured the head. After being taken to hospital the same day, death was confirmed.

In construction work to temporarily dismantle a shrine's existing fence (tamagaki) and rebuild it from the foundation, while the victim was excavating soil under the foundation of a free-standing main post (23 cm wide × 196 cm high, weighing about 340 kg) with a square shovel, the post fell toward the victim, who was pinned under it. The victim was a technical intern trainee.

At a demolition site for a wooden house, the victim, who was erecting single pipes assembled in a grid pattern and stretching protective sheeting on them to prevent debris from scattering to the neighboring property (at a height of 2 m or more), fell.

While the victim alone was performing maintenance inspection of cubicle-type high-voltage power receiving equipment and a solar system in the factory of an establishment under an electrical safety service contract, the victim stepped through the glass (wired plate glass, t = 6.8 mm) of a skylight window, installed at about 5 m intervals in the factory ceiling, and fell to the concrete floor about 17.0 m below.

At a repair site for a road fence beside a prefectural road with two lanes in each direction, the left lane was closed starting about 50 m before the work site, and three construction vehicles were parked on the road within the closed area. A 4-tonne Unic truck (truck crane) traveling on the road entered the closed area, struck a traffic guard, and then rear-ended the lead construction vehicle. The traffic guard died as a result of this accident.

In the warehouse of a building materials store, after finishing stacking steel pipes, a meeting was being held about the next task when the binding band (steel strapping) of the bottom-tier steel pipes slipped out of its seal (binding clip), and the bound pipes (97 pipes, 1.58 tonnes) collapsed. As a result, nine bundles of steel pipes (about 7 tonnes) stacked on top fell forward, and the victim, who was in front, was pinned under them.

In the AL plant on the establishment's premises, to clean a tank used for manufacturing agricultural chemical formulations (diameter 1.8 m, depth 3.263 m), the victim was spraying cleaning fluid (containing xylene and ethylbenzene) into the tank with a nozzle hose through the manhole at the top of the tank when an explosion and fire occurred, and the victim suffered burns over the whole body. The victim was treated at the hospital to which the victim was taken, but died.

While driving straight along a national highway in a light truck to deliver newspapers, the victim collided with a truck (refrigerated vehicle) that turned right from the oncoming lane (a right-turn-only lane before an intersection) to enter a convenience store.

When delivering materials for construction to a road construction site, a truck driver who had removed the truck sheet on the bed of a dump truck fell and sustained a head injury. After being taken by ambulance, the victim died while hospitalized for treatment.

After finishing work at the site, while traveling on a prefectural road in a small cargo truck, the vehicle crossed the center line on a right curve in a tunnel and collided head-on with an oncoming vehicle.

After finishing work at the site, while traveling on a prefectural road in a small cargo truck, the vehicle crossed the center line on a right curve in a tunnel and collided head-on with an oncoming vehicle.

On the 3rd floor of a building, while the victim and co-workers were pushing a display vehicle by hand from a car lift into the building, the victim fell from the edge of the car lift to a pit on the 2nd basement level about 20 m below, and died.

While on the way from the head office to a delivery destination by truck to transport cargo, a tire burst just before a tunnel. The victim turned on the hazard lights and slowed down, but ended up inside the tunnel and stopped as far to the left of the travel lane as possible. The victim got out, checked the tire, and while phoning the company, immediately tried to take the warning triangle from the passenger seat, at which point the truck was rear-ended by a large truck coming from behind.

The victim was engaged in dormitory management duties (patrols, managing mail, etc.) as an assistant dormitory staff member. On the day of the accident, the dormitory manager, having noticed that the victim was unwell, instructed the victim not to work and to sit and wait for a replacement to arrive, and left for another task. A replacement later arrived, but the victim could not be seen, so the dormitory was searched and the victim was found lying, bleeding from the head, on the landing in front of the stairs on the 1st basement floor.

Grass cutting was being carried out around a noise barrier with one lane of a road with two lanes in each direction closed. Partway along the lane closure there was an exit ramp side road, and the lane closure had been lifted there to allow passage. The victim was alerting passing vehicles at the tip of the divergence where the lane closure resumed. The victim was struck by a truck traveling in the closed lane.

Because a malfunction occurred in an injection molding machine, the victim was repeatedly entering and leaving the danger zone of the machine to lubricate it. While the victim was inside the danger zone, worker A, who was working with the victim, mistakenly lowered the slide, and the victim's whole body was caught in the injection molding machine, and the victim died.
In a fishing port, the victim, who was walking toward a sorting table to sort landed fish, was struck by a forklift (maximum load 2.5 t) traveling forward in the port, and died.

A passerby found the victim, who had been delivering newspapers in the early morning, lying face up in front of the approach stairs of an apartment building where delivery had been completed, and death was subsequently confirmed. The victim's blood remained on the top step of the approach stairs, and the bicycle the victim used for delivery was left beside the stairs.

A worker at a road construction site complained of feeling unwell during work and was resting lying down in a parking lot near the site. When the worker stood up for some reason, the worker lost balance, fell, and struck the back of the head on the asphalt ground. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance and underwent surgery, but subsequently died.

At a site for repair of a cross pipe, during road surface excavation, the victim was doing assisting work between the excavator (backhoe) bucket and a compaction machine on the operator's instructions, and the operator was moving the excavator forward little by little toward the victim. The operator stopped the excavator, but the machine slid forward due to ground conditions, and as a result the victim, who was between the excavator bucket and the compaction machine, was caught between the bucket and the compaction machine.

During inspection work with a lane closed inside a tunnel on a general national highway, a work vehicle reversing within the closed area struck the victim. After the accident, the victim was taken to hospital by doctor helicopter and died while hospitalized for treatment.

At a site visited on a business trip, when the victim stopped the truck for unloading and opened the rear double doors, palletized cargo (about 220 kg) fell and struck the victim, who fell over and was injured. The victim was receiving treatment for a neck fracture and spinal cord injury, but died.

While the victim was riding a 125 cc motorcycle on a municipal road to deliver newspapers, the victim for some reason lost balance and fell down a slope beside the road (about 2.2 m high), was pinned under the motorcycle, and died of asphyxia due to neck compression. At the time of the accident, the area near the site was fully closed to vehicles due to road widening work, and only a pedestrian walkway (about 70 cm wide) was provided.

While the victim was restacking goods using a 75 cm high step stool in the establishment's warehouse, the victim fell from the step stool and struck the head hard on the concrete floor. The victim was taken by ambulance, underwent a craniotomy, and was hospitalized in the intensive care unit, but died of brain contusion.

The victim, the business owner, and a co-worker, three people in total, were removing trees that had fallen due to heavy rain. To remove a tree that had fallen onto the roof of a private house, the victim was cutting off branches on the roof while the tree was suspended by an excavator (backhoe) operated by the business owner, when the victim slipped and nearly fell. The business owner immediately lowered the arm to try to stop the victim with the excavator bucket, whereupon the suspended tree struck the victim's abdomen, and the victim subsequently died.

Replacement work on a flight conveyor in a factory. During assembly of temporary scaffolding on the 3rd floor of the factory, the victim was moving by ducking under a single-pipe guardrail for fall prevention when the victim stepped into an opening covered with flame-retardant sheeting and fell together with the sheeting 13 m to the factory's 1st floor.

To attach a screw to the hydraulic system of a forklift, the victim placed a single piece of timber (10.2 cm wide × 3 cm thick × 138.5 cm high) under the raised forks as a safety prop, then reduced the hydraulic pressure of the hydraulic system while under the forks. The timber supporting the forks broke, the forks fell onto the victim, and the victim died.

Heavy rain from the morning caused the natural ground around a tunnel to collapse, resulting in a landslide. The victim went missing. During a search for missing persons by the Self-Defense Forces, fire department, and police, the victim was found pinned under an office car that had been overturned by the landslide on the detour at the Wajima-side entrance of the tunnel, and death was confirmed.

While delivering morning newspapers on a motorized bicycle (moped), the victim was waiting at a traffic signal at an intersection when rear-ended by a passenger car. The victim remained unconscious thereafter and died of severe head trauma.

The victim was feeding peat moss, a raw material for fertilizer, into a mixer. Because no lid, enclosure, fence, or the like was provided at the opening, the worker fell through the opening, was caught in the screw, and died.

In road construction work, during well drilling, the victim was bothered by iron powder adhering to the lower part of the drilling machine and bent forward to check it, whereupon the victim's head was caught in a moving part of the drilling machine, and the victim died of brain contusion.
The victim took part in snorkeling at a company-sponsored event and died by drowning offshore, 100 m from land.
During sewer pipe rehabilitation work, localized heavy rain occurred, the water level in the pipe rose rapidly, and the victims were swept away. The bodies were later found in a river.
During sewer pipe rehabilitation work, localized heavy rain occurred, the water level in the pipe rose rapidly, and the victims were swept away. The bodies were later found in a river.
The victim, who was removing linens dried in a dryer from the dryer, was found with burns in front of the dryer's unloading opening.

At a 2-story private house, current leakage was found in the section of wiring running across the roof, on the route from the service drop at the utility pole to the house's distribution board, and the plan was to cut out that section and install a separate new route along the eaves of the house to the distribution board. When the victim tried to measure the dimensions of the planned installation location at the eaves for an estimate, the victim contacted an energized part of the roof and was electrocuted. The roof was wooden, but iron parts and nails were used for reinforcement.

During removal of ready-mixed concrete from the delivery pipe of a concrete pump truck, a cleaning ball was inserted into the delivery pipe from the pump truck side and compressed air was sent into the pipe, pushing the concrete out with the cleaning ball. The victim, who was checking the position of the cleaning ball by tapping the pipe with a ratchet wrench, moved near the hose attached to the end of the pipe, whereupon white smoke and the cleaning ball shot out of the end of the hose, and the victim was struck by the hose, which swung from the recoil.

While the victim was traveling in the passing lane, a medium-size vehicle that changed from the travel lane into the passing lane struck the left front of the vehicle driven by the victim. The recoil sent the victim's vehicle flying, and it collided with a trailer stopped due to breakdown in an emergency parking zone ahead on the right. As a result, the victim was caught in the truck cab and died of aortic injury.

The victim, who was performing inspection work alone in a solar power plant, did not return to the office after the end of working hours, so a search was carried out but the victim could not be found. Later, the victim was found dead, lying face down next to a utility pole installed in a thicket on the plant premises.

At a golf course, a worker doing course maintenance was operating a top dressing machine (a ride-on machine that spreads sand on turf) and climbing a paved cart path (gradient about 15 degrees) to move between holes, when the machine tipped over backward (a so-called wheelie) and the worker was pinned under it.

The victim, together with a worker from a partner company (two people), was marking important plant species at risk of being affected, growing on steep terrain with an average gradient of about 45 degrees, for a planned geological survey near a tunnel, when the victim slid and fell.

For roof repair work on a private house (2-story wooden building), no scaffold was installed around the house, and the victim was made to go up onto the 2nd-floor roof and do painting work without being provided with a safety helmet or a fall arrest device meeting performance requirements. When a resident of the house went out the front door, the resident found the victim lying with blood flowing from the head and called an ambulance. Death was subsequently confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.
While burying solar power cables (depth about 1.3 m), the excavation face collapsed, and the victim was struck by collapsed asphalt and concrete fragments made of crushed slag.
While the victim was towing a broken-down vehicle on the shoulder of the outbound lanes of an expressway, the victim was hit by a truck and died.

The victim drove a 2-tonne truck (electric vehicle) in reverse up a slope and stopped in front of the delivery destination. When the victim got out of the truck to place wheel chocks, the truck started to run away. The victim clung to the driver's door and ran alongside the truck to try to stop it, was caught between the truck and the wall of a house, and died of multiple injuries.
Because the LED lamp at the upper inspection window of a plastic crusher had burned out, the victim was inspecting the lamp and was electrocuted.

To prepare an estimate for a vehicle inspection, the victim placed a car (gross vehicle weight: 2,665 kg) on a two-post lift (maximum load capacity: 3,200 kg) and was inspecting the car (working alone), when for some reason one of the lift arms supporting the car body shifted, the car body became unbalanced, fell off the lift and overturned, and the victim, who was nearby, was pinned under it.

The victim started work alone to clean drainage catch basins (3 locations) outside the factory (on the establishment's premises). The same day, a co-worker, worried that the victim had not returned, looked at the victim's planned work area from the window of the break room in the factory and found the victim with the upper body inside the catch basin being worked on. The co-worker hurriedly rescued the victim, but the victim was no longer breathing, and death was confirmed the same day at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

At a bridge foundation construction site, during press-in of steel sheet piles with a pile driver (crush piler), the victim approached the pile driver to clean the area welded to temporarily fix the sheet pile to the pile driver before setting the next sheet pile, and the victim's head was caught in a moving part of the pile driver.

At a recycled crushed stone plant, during crushing of concrete rubble to the specified size, the victim was found caught between the roller section of a belt conveyor in the crushing equipment and the ground. The roller section was removed and the victim was rescued, but death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.
While on a business trip, walking to a meeting location, the victim was crossing near a crosswalk without traffic signals when struck by a car coming from the victim's right.

During floor plate repair work on an edible oil tank, when the victim tried to weld a steel plate to serve as the floor plate, an explosion occurred inside the tank, and the victim died from the impact. Immediately before the welding, a cleaning agent containing hazardous materials (flammable substances) had been used to clean edible oil adhering to the surface of the steel plate during the process leading up to welding.

During sewer pipe laying work in an intersection, three workers were working in a vertical shaft about 2.5 m square and about 3 m deep set up in the intersection, when the excavation face, wetted by water from a water pipe cut for the work, collapsed and soil flowed into the shaft. Two workers were buried in the soil, and one died.

While cleaning incineration ash inside an incinerator, the victim fell from the end of the flue between the incinerator and the secondary combustion chamber into the secondary combustion chamber about 10 m below, was taken to a medical institution, and died the same day.

A municipal road leading to the construction site (about 3.6 m wide, gravel) had been damaged by heavy rain and was impeding vehicle traffic, so restoration work such as spreading crushed stone was being carried out. Because the road was narrow and there was no place to turn around, it had been decided that a dump truck (4 t) would reverse to the locations where crushed stone was to be spread and dump the stone at several points. The victim was run over by the dump truck while it was reversing, and died.

Near the east wall of a factory's monitor (roof monitor), the victim was supervising two workers re-cladding the east wall of the monitor when the victim stepped through the large roof near the east wall and fell to the ground inside the No. 3 factory about 17 m below. The victim was taken to hospital but subsequently died.

Work was being carried out to excavate a cylindrical shaft 2.0 m in diameter to construct foundation piles for a bridge abutment. An excavator (backhoe) with a bucket capacity of 0.01 m3 (machine weight 0.45 tonnes) had been lowered into the shaft, and the victim was operating it alone to excavate the bottom, etc. A site staff member of the prime contractor who came to check the site found the victim in the shaft with the left arm and chest caught between a bar of the excavator operator's seat and the liner plates used for earth retaining.

While traveling on the inbound lanes of an expressway, traffic congestion occurred near where the road narrowed to one lane due to construction. A vehicle coming from behind rear-ended the victim's vehicle, which was at the end of the queue, pushing it forward, and the impact caused it to rear-end the truck ahead.

During renewal work on electrical equipment, cables were being pulled in from outdoors into the building through buried conduits and the like. While the victim on the 2nd floor of the building was pulling in the rope tied to the cables with an electric winch, a pulley that had been fixed to the floor with anchor bolts and used for pulling in the rope came loose and struck the left chest of the victim, who was operating the electric winch at a position about 17 m away.

A worker who was collecting river garbage using a garbage collection boat fell from the boat and drowned. The person who moored the boat before a break was different from the person who unmoored it after the break, and although the boat had been moored at three points, it set out with only two points released, so the boat stopped suddenly and the victim, who was at the front end of the boat, fell into the river from the recoil.

At a construction site for an erosion control (sabo) dam, the victim was cutting a standing tree 15 cm in diameter and 15 m tall that was obstructing the work, using a chainsaw from the uphill side of the tree, when the tree being cut split vertically and struck the victim's head.

In a rental warehouse, the victim was replacing a light bulb while standing on top of pallets (45 pallets) raised by a forklift (about 8 m above the floor) when the pallets collapsed, and the victim fell to the concrete floor and died.

To perform ceiling wiring work in connection with electrical wiring for renovation inside a commercial building, the victim was standing on a mobile scaffold (work platform height 1,075 mm, long side 1,571 mm, short side 1,022 mm) and was about to receive a tool for threading cables, sent by a co-worker, when the victim fell to the long side together with the scaffold. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance but died. The scaffold was fitted with sensing frames to indicate the edges of the work platform.

While the victim alone was repairing the inside of the discharge outlet of a concrete bucket (capacity 6 m3) used for placing concrete in a dam body (arc welding steel flat bars 9 mm thick and 25 mm wide), the victim's chest and back were caught in the discharge outlet, and the victim died of aortic injury and compression of the chest and back.

During rooftop waterproofing renovation work at an elementary school, the victim fell while peeling off PVC sheeting on the 3rd-floor roof (height 11.0 m), and died. Around the work surface of the 3rd-floor roof where the victim was working, there was a parapet 36.5 cm high, but no guardrails or other fall prevention equipment had been installed.

At a demolition site associated with new construction, the victim was scraping off soil adhering to steel sheet piles at ground level between the sheet piles and the existing basement exterior wall (about 3 m below the surface). The victim instructed the heavy equipment operator on the surface by radio to excavate soil. The operator asked by radio whether further excavation was needed but there was no response, and on getting off the machine to check, found the victim lying down. Because of the height difference and the exterior wall of the existing building, the victim and the operator were not able to see each other.

The victim was caught in the crushing unit of a volume reduction machine (a machine that crushes, melts, and extrudes waste polystyrene foam) that started unexpectedly. The victim had put the upper body inside the crushing unit and was trying to retrieve, with fire tongs, a blade of the crushing unit that had broken and dropped to the position of the screw. A co-worker who was assisting mistakenly started the crushing unit (pressing the wrong start button), and the victim was caught in the crushing unit.

While transporting system kitchen equipment on a truck, the victim had stopped on the shoulder of the outbound lanes of an expressway due to a vehicle breakdown when rear-ended by a large truck from behind, and died.
The victim was found dead inside a factory wastewater storage tank. The tank was made of concrete; its top could be reached by external stairs, and an opening into the tank was provided on the top.

At a hospital, a co-worker, worried that the victim had not come to the meeting place after the lunch break, checked the victim's car parked in the parking lot on the establishment's premises and found the victim lying beside the car, bleeding from the head. The victim was taken by ambulance, but death was confirmed the same day.

During road pavement repair work, while worker A was operating a roller to compact soil, the victim, who had entered the travel area for some reason such as taking site photographs for records, was run over and died. At the time of the accident, A intended to compact a 3.7 m wide municipal road by running the roller back and forth 3 or 4 times, and before reversing on the 1st and 2nd passes confirmed that the victim was on the ridge between the road and a rice paddy, but failed to check the victim's position before reversing on the 3rd or 4th pass.

A waste hauler brought in plastic waste by garbage truck. The plan was to unload at a location designated on the instructions of the factory's guide, but the truck was reversing into the factory without a signal from the guide, and the guide, who was near the entrance confirming the unloading location by radio with workers inside the factory, was run over.

While the victim and another person (two people) were lifting rubber material (about 30 kg) on a pallet and moving it to a cart, the victim lost footing on the pallet, fell backward, and struck the head on the floor. After the injury, the victim was hospitalized for treatment, but died.

A health checkup was being held in a meeting room on the 2nd floor. After the checkup ended, the victim was carrying a desk alone down the stairs, caught a foot on a leg of the desk, and as a result fell to the ground, struck the head hard, and was injured.

The victim was found dead by a co-worker in the sleeper berth in the truck cab. The direct cause of death was asphyxia, and the cause of the asphyxia was heatstroke. While loading the truck, the victim developed heatstroke, which was accompanied by regurgitation of drinking water and its entry into the trachea and bronchi, causing asphyxia that led to death. During the work, the victim wore an air-conditioned (fan-equipped) garment; the estimated WBGT value was around 27. On that day, loading work took place only at the establishment where the accident occurred, and at other times the victim was engaged in truck inspection work.

After finishing work in the 2nd-floor workplace, the victim went down the stairs to the 1st-floor workplace for work on the 1st floor, carrying two aprons and a garbage bag containing mainly plastic bags and other trash. Because the victim, who should have gone down first, did not come to the meeting place, the route was searched, and the victim was found lying on the landing of the stairs leading from the 1st floor to the basement. The victim was then taken to hospital, where death was confirmed.

The establishment was a culvert construction site. Victims A and B, two people, entered the excavated area where pipes were to be laid and were leveling the bottom when the soil of the side wall collapsed and both were buried alive.
