A died and B was injured. The area entered had an excavation depth of about 4.2 m and a width of 1.2 m.

At a demolition site for a 9-story building, beams on the 6th floor were being separated using demolition shears. For some reason, an exterior wall board broke through a soundproof panel and fell outside the scaffold, striking a male traffic guard from the site who was cleaning fallen leaves and the like on the roadway. The victim was taken to hospital unconscious but died on the day of the accident.

While the victim was cleaning up deposits (metal scale, etc.) in an underground pit, an iron partition plate (about 1 m wide, about 1 m high, weighing about 180 kg) installed on top of a concrete partition wall (80 cm high, 40 cm thick) in the pit fell over, and the victim was pinned under it and died.

In a rice husk storehouse, while the victim was treading on rice husks to make them fall toward the discharge conveyor, the husks the victim was standing on collapsed, and the victim was carried away by the husks and buried.

The victim and six other related workers were laying power cables (cable drums) on the 5th-floor outdoor floor of Company A's No. 4 boiler, as preparatory work for spraying refractory material on the inner surface of the straight body of a cyclone. The victim entered a restricted area where walkways and handrails were under construction, approached an opening, and fell 9 m to the 4th floor.

The victim was driving a truck to a shipper's location. After entering at an interchange and traveling on the outbound lanes of an expressway, the truck skidded and crashed into the median strip. The victim was taken to hospital but died.

Broke (waste paper) occurred at the drying section of a production line and was removed. When the machine was restarted, the victim had not evacuated to a safe place, the victim's left leg was caught, and the victim died of massive blood loss.

Two people including the victim were checking, in preparation for an approaching typhoon, the tightness of scaffold connections and the flame-retardant sheeting that had been hung so as not to damage electric wires and the like. While the two were tucking the sheeting between the scaffold standards and a crossarm extending from the building to keep it from blowing away, for some reason only the victim was electrocuted.

The establishment was a sabo (erosion control) weir construction site. The victim and co-worker A, two people, were surveying on the riverbank for diverting the river. The victim tried to go to the opposite bank, entered the river at a point where it was about 20 m wide, and while crossing was swept away at a point about 1 m deep. One hour after being swept away, the victim was found in cardiopulmonary arrest about 2 km downstream of the site and was taken to a hospital in the city, but died.

The victim was operating an overhead crane (radio-controlled) alone to move bundled steel (bars) to a cutting machine, and was found caught between the steel suspended by the crane and a handrail; death was confirmed.

On a nearly straight section of an expressway with one lane in each direction, while the victim was driving a company car, a large truck crossed over from the oncoming lane and collided head-on with the company car, and the victim died.

On a hull block in a shipyard, the victim was carrying scaffold materials when the victim suddenly collapsed during the work and was taken by ambulance. The victim died the next day at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

While the victim was traveling in a wagon to a client's home for a home-visit nursing call, the victim collided head-on on the road with a trailer from the oncoming lane, and died. The victim was driving alone, with no passengers.
A following truck rear-ended the vehicle driven by the victim, which was stopped at the end of a traffic queue.

While driving a trailer to carry waste corrugated cardboard to a port, the victim failed to negotiate a sharp left curve, ran off the road, and overturned. The victim was trapped in the driver's seat of the tractor head and was later rescued, but death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

After replacing the grinding wheel of a grinding machine and adjusting the guard, adjustment piece, and work rest, the worker was grinding off unwanted parts of a casting when the grinding wheel (50 cm diameter, 5 cm wide) suddenly burst, a blast came through a gap in the guard, and the worker doing the grinding was blown 4 m 70 cm.

To replace a lighting pole beside a road, a pole (diameter 250 mm, height 10-12 m) was being installed using a mobile crane when the nylon sling used for slinging came off, the pole fell, and the victim on the ground was pinned under it.

The victim and a co-worker, two people, were painting to renovate a vacant unit in a housing complex and were each taking a break in separate cars. When the co-worker checked on the victim, the co-worker found the victim had vomited in the car and called an ambulance, but death was confirmed at the medical institution to which the victim was taken.

The victim, who was performing maintenance on a water intake channel for power generation, fell while moving from the right bank to the left bank of a river to check the intake flow measuring device and other equipment on the left bank. After falling, the victim was swept away by the swollen river and, with a body-belt-type fall arrest device attached to a lifeline, was continuously struck by water at a waterfall-like section of the weir, causing the body to be swung about, and the head, torso, and other parts were repeatedly struck against the weir.

The victim climbed onto a slate roof to repair the roof of a warehouse located at the above address, stepped through the slate roof, and fell into the warehouse. At the time of the accident, no walkway boards had been installed on the roof, and the victim was not using a safety helmet or fall arrest device.

It is presumed that the victim, who was providing security at a school, fell inside a building and injured the face and head. After the injury, the victim was conscious and drove home in the victim's own car. The next day, because the victim could not be contacted, a person in charge from the establishment visited the victim's home and found the victim dead in the living room, with blood flowing from the face.

During foundation expansion work on power plant premises, while reversing a crawler carrier (off-road transport vehicle) under a pipe (steel pipe) to transport soil, the victim's head was caught between the steel pipe and the vehicle's handrail. The operator's seat of the crawler carrier is outside, and in a normal posture the operator's upper body protrudes above the vehicle height.

An agricultural machine (a combine harvester) had been lifted with a hydraulic jack, and while the victim was underneath it in that state performing maintenance work, the hydraulic jack came off for some reason and the victim was caught between the ground and the machine. The victim was rescued immediately after being found, but death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was transported.

The victim was traveling by passenger car on an expressway to go to a partner company. Six people were riding in a seven-seat passenger car, and the victim was seated on the right side of the second row. On the way, the car encountered congestion caused by roadworks and stopped with its hazard lights flashing. A few minutes after stopping, it was rear-ended by a passenger car approaching from behind.
While delivering boxed lunches (bento), the victim was involved in a single-vehicle traffic accident. The victim died later while receiving treatment in hospital.

After reading gas meters, the victim was returning to the office by bicycle and approached an intersection with neither traffic signals nor a pedestrian crossing (one lane in each direction, with a right-turn lane). Attempting to cross the intersection, the victim passed between a line of vehicles stopped in the near lane (through/left-turn lane) and entered the right-turn lane, where the victim was struck by a 2-ton truck traveling in the right-turn lane and hit their head hard on the ground. The victim was immediately transported to a medical facility, where death was confirmed.

While running wiring from a storage battery to a transformer (cubicle: width 2 m, length 4.83 m, height 1.92 m) in order to check energization of the battery, the victim's left elbow came into contact with an iron plate inside the transformer leading from a breaker, and the victim received an electric shock. The iron plate was 8 cm wide, 80 cm long, and 1 cm, and the voltage at the time of the accident was 200 V.

During construction work to lay a drainage ditch 47.5 m in total length, the victim was performing auxiliary work. While the victim was doing cleanup work, the foreman noticed something was wrong; the victim did not respond when spoken to and appeared to be in distress, so the victim was transported by ambulance. The victim had been hospitalized in an unconscious state since the time of the incident and died at the hospital.

The victim, who had been doing tree-felling work, and one other worker were heading to the work site after a break; because that worker was preparing machinery and other items, the victim went ahead to the site alone. When the worker arrived at the site later, the worker found the victim lying collapsed at the bottom of a mountain slope.

The victim was a custodian employed at a high school. While weeding alone near an irrigation channel that flows through the school grounds, the victim tumbled down the slope of an embankment and fell into the channel, was swept away and went missing, and was found the next day downstream in the channel.

A worker of a primary subcontractor working at a site constructing an emergency exit (vertical shaft) for the Shinkansen took time off due to symptoms such as hand cramps; afterwards the worker's condition recovered and the worker resumed work. After finishing work and arriving at the company by car, the worker lost consciousness upon changing to another vehicle to go home. After being taken to hospital, the worker's death was confirmed.

To load and unload formwork materials, the victim, standing on the bed of a vehicle-mounted truck crane, slung a bundle of square steel pipes (30 cm x 60 cm x 4 m) and then was taking a phone call with their back to the load, when the mobile crane operator performed a hoisting operation by remote control; the load, once lifted off the ground, moved and struck the victim, and the victim fell from the truck bed and was killed. The victim was wearing a fall-protection helmet at the time of the fall.

Intending to repair a photoelectric (light-beam) sensor installed inside a conveyor, the victim entered the conveyor and had their upper body sticking out through a gap between carrier rolls traveling along the upper part of the conveyor, with a fixed shaft against their chest, when a carrier roll coming from behind caught the victim between it and the shaft, and the victim died.

The victim and a coworker were waiting their turn in two dump trucks at the edge of the yard where the accident occurred, in order to load quarried stone. The victim told the coworker they were going to the toilet, got out of the truck and went to the toilet, but did not return, so a search of the vicinity was made with other workers, and the victim was found dead in a settling pond about 20 m below the yard. Between the edge of the yard and the settling pond there is an earth embankment 90 cm to 100 cm high, and the slope has an inclination of about 90 degrees.
While delivering newspapers on a moped, the victim attempted to turn right on a national highway and collided head-on with a motorcycle going straight in the opposite lane.

The victim was working in the factory together with one other coworker. The coworker, who was working at a different location from the victim, heard a splashing sound ('bochan'); looking in the direction of the sound, the coworker could not see the victim, and on checking inside a tank in that direction used for soaking timber in water (estimated water temperature 60°C), found the victim floating face down.

After work ended on the day before the accident, the car of a freight elevator in a warehouse was landed at the mezzanine floor, and a piece of square timber about 3 m long was placed in the hoistway as a measure to prevent the car from falling. At the start of work on the day of the accident, when the victim attempted to remove the timber in order to use the elevator, the car fell and the victim was trapped underneath it.

The victim was working alone, felling oak trees with a chainsaw. The team leader, finding it suspicious that the victim had not taken a single break, went with a worker to check on the victim and found the victim lying collapsed. When found, an oak tree with a diameter at breast height of 22 cm and a total length of about 24 m was lying over the victim's neck, and the oak had split at a point 1 m 10 cm from its base.

Three workers including the victim had been pruning garden trees at a detached house since the morning. In the afternoon, the victim was pruning the hedge in front of the entrance while the other two workers were pruning the plantings beside the entrance. On hearing a loud noise from the direction of the entrance, the other workers went there and found the victim lying on the road beneath a stepladder (top plate height about 2.8 m) that had been set up on the road in front of the entrance. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet.

A worker employed on a day-labor contract doing picking work in a warehouse complained of feeling unwell and rested in the break room for about an hour. While moving from the break room to the work area, the worker fell backward on a staircase, struck the back of the head hard, and died of cerebral contusion.

At a swimming beach, while the victim was working as an attendant watching over bathers, a male bather swimming in the sea appeared to have been swept away by the waves, so the victim entered the sea to rescue him and drowned.

During repair work on the partition plates of an aggregate storage bin in a ready-mixed concrete plant, a worker lay prone and picked up a floodlight to look into the storage bin, whereupon the worker groaned and appeared to go rigid. When another worker unplugged the extension cord connected to the floodlight from a 100 V outlet, the rigidity released and the worker fell into the storage bin (depth about 2.2 m). The worker was then transported to a medical facility, where death was confirmed, and it was later determined that the cause of death was electrocution.

While the victim was cleaning a dump truck with its bed raised, the bed came down and the victim's upper body was caught between the mudguard attached to the bed and the right rear wheel of the dump truck, and the victim died of traumatic asphyxia.
While pruning rose bushes in a cemetery, the victim was stung in multiple places by yellow hornets nesting nearby and died from anaphylactic shock.

Three people, one forklift operator and two others including the victim, were wrapping a container lifted 1.6 m high by a forklift (wrapping it with plastic film so that the parts inside would not fall out), when the container fell toward the victim and struck the victim. The container measured 1.8 m (long side) x 1.3 m (short side) x 1.5 m high, was packed with multiple machine tool parts (frames, etc.), and weighed about 1 t in total.

During equipment renewal work at a station, an aerial work platform was positioned on the road, and the victim and two others were on its work platform, inspecting the interior while successively removing exterior wall panels from the lower part of the station. The victim, who was operating the platform while leaning out from inside the work platform, was caught at the neck between an exterior wall panel and the handrail of the work platform, and died.

The victim was assisting with instruction in a moped training course on an outdoor asphalt course (temperature about 40 degrees). During a break, while walking to the office, the victim staggered, and a nearby staff member supported the victim; as the victim's consciousness was clouded, an ambulance was called, but the victim died after being transported to hospital.
While towing a broken-down vehicle on the shoulder of the inbound lanes of an expressway, the victim was struck by a trailer coming from behind and died.

While performing traffic control as support personnel at a road improvement construction site, the victim collapsed after feeling unwell, was taken to hospital by ambulance, and then died of heatstroke.

The victim was working in a factory but, feeling unwell, was going to leave early and went to the changing room. When a coworker entered the changing room, the coworker found the victim collapsed; the victim was transported to hospital, where death was confirmed.

A perpetrator who had been sitting in the innermost chair on the first floor of the store trying on a watch took out a knife in an attempt to steal the watch and ran toward the store exit. The victim, who heard the commotion near the exit inside the store, leaned out to see what was happening and ended up in the perpetrator's path; when they collided, the victim was stabbed in the abdomen and subsequently died of blood loss.

On the business premises, the victim was replacing an attachment (lower guide) of a foundation construction machine. In doing this work, a rod held by the auger was being raised to 2.2 m above ground level (GL), when the rod came free of the catch and fell onto the victim's head.

A load of aluminum material kept outside the factory (divided across three-tier racks, about 700 kg in total, load height about 180 cm, length about 460 cm) was placed on a dolly with a forklift, and three workers were moving the dolly into the factory when the load collapsed, and the worker guiding the front of the load was trapped beneath it.

On a wheel production line, a crane used to transport wheels stopped traveling under its own power. To move the crane to the maintenance position, the victim entered the work zone of a grinder robot on the production line and was pulling the crane's hoisting chain, when a conveying device within that work zone started moving and the victim was caught at the lower back and other areas between the equipment and the conveying device.

The victim, who was working as a security guard at a construction site within a traffic-restricted zone on a road, was walking within the restricted zone to leave as the day's work and cleanup at the site were nearly finished, when a motorcycle that had entered without following vehicle guidance struck the victim from behind.

After finishing traffic control duties for drainage pipe work associated with land development works, the victim headed home in a commuting vehicle and crashed into the outer wall of a private house 50 m from the construction site. The victim was conscious but died at the medical facility to which the victim was transported.

At the workplace, while unloading an empty gas cylinder (weighing about 50 kg) collected from a customer from a truck bed onto a platform, the victim suddenly felt ill and slowly collapsed on the spot. Coworkers nearby called for an ambulance, but death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was transported. (Heatstroke)
While delivering evening newspapers, the victim felt ill with symptoms considered to be heatstroke and was transported to hospital by ambulance, but died the same day.

To trim branches of trees encroaching on a power transmission line, the victim and the foreman were aboard the bucket of an aerial work platform, cutting branches. The cut branches were being collected in the bucket, and when the bucket became full of branches, the victim operated the controls on the bucket and swung the boom to lower the branches to the ground, during which the victim came into contact with a distribution line (6,600 V) at a height of about 8.7 m and was electrocuted.

On that day the victim came to the office and, after taking out the garbage, was mowing grass on an embankment about 75 m from the office. A truck driver traveling on the farm road leading to the office loading entrance found the victim lying face down on top of the embankment. When found, the victim was already unconscious and was in cardiopulmonary arrest when the fire department arrived. Death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was transported.

On a forest road near the workplace, three people including the victim were felling standing trees. After the victim and a coworker had delimbed a standing tree 8.6 m tall, the victim made a cut with a chainsaw at a height of 0.8 m from the base of the tree, whereupon the tree fell and struck the victim near the back as the victim was trying to move out of the way.
On a prefectural road, a worker performing traffic control for alternating one-way traffic associated with pruning of roadside trees was run over by a passenger car and died.

While the victim was sorting H-beams for shipment, the lifting clamp suspended from the hook of the hoist-type overhead crane (rated load 2.83 t) that the victim was operating caught on stacked H-beams (500 x 200 x 10 x 16 mm, weight 1,058 kg), and three H-beams fell and struck the victim. The victim had been recovering after surgery but died.

At the time of the accident, at the shipper's premises, scrap was being loaded onto the bed of a large trailer using a demolition grapple (operated by a worker of the shipper). The victim had climbed onto the trailer bed and was checking the loading of the scrap when the victim came into contact with scrap held by the demolition grapple, and as a result fell about 4 m from the trailer bed.

The victim, who had been collecting baking trays at the exit of a bake-off oven, came staggering into the materials room. Judging it to be heatstroke, others cooled the victim's body, but the victim lost consciousness and an ambulance was requested. The victim went into cardiopulmonary arrest during transport, and despite resuscitation efforts at the receiving medical facility, died.
A dispatched worker, while moving within a warehouse at an off-site location where the worker was doing inspection work, was run over by a forklift reversing from the right rear, and died.

At the shipper's premises, the victim was waiting beside a truck while checking (monitoring) the unloading of timber from the truck bed by forklift, when the band binding a bundle of timber (weight 3.6 t) lifted by the forklift broke and several pieces of timber fell from the bundle to the ground. At the moment the victim approached to pick them up, all the timber being lifted by the forklift collapsed, and the victim was trapped underneath and died.

The victim operated a thread-cutting machine for machining bicycle wheel axles in a prefabricated factory with a corrugated-sheet roof that had no equipment for cooling the work area, and had continued working in the hot work environment every day except Saturdays and Sundays. After finishing work, the victim rode a bicycle to the nearest station, but was found in the station's bicycle parking area slumped face down over the bicycle and unable to move. The victim was promptly transported to hospital but died.
While mowing grass with a grass cutter on the slope of a riverbank outside the premises, the victim fell from an embankment about 5 m high.

The victim was waiting in a stopped trailer beside the container lane to receive a container unloaded ashore, when the spreader of a rubber-tired gantry crane struck container 4E in the figure; container 4E toppled over and pushed out container 3F, which collapsed and fell, and the tractor unit (trailer head) was crushed beneath it, trapping the victim.

While working with a Banbury mixer (a machine that melts and spreads resin), for some reason the victim's entire body was caught in the rotating part of the machine. The work the victim was doing immediately before the accident is unknown.

The victim was transporting a cart (self-weight 7 t) with a traverser. After moving the traverser to the designated position, while unloading the cart from the traverser, the victim forgot to attach the runaway-prevention wire, so the unloaded cart ran away. Noticing the runaway, the victim went around to the front of the cart and tried to stop it by hand, but it did not stop and the victim was trapped underneath the cart.

The victim was driving a semi-medium-sized cargo vehicle on a prefectural road when a standard-sized passenger vehicle in the oncoming lane spun, crossed over the median strip, and collided with the victim's vehicle. The victim was then transported to hospital, where death was confirmed.

The victim and coworker A were storing an agricultural implement, which they had processed on order from a ranch owner, in a designated cowshed. At the entrance of the cowshed, the victim was guiding a tractor driven by A, towing the implement, as it reversed, when the victim was stung by a bee or wasp. After being stung, the victim drove a truck alone toward the nearest hospital but went off the side of the road on the way. The victim was found unconscious in the truck and taken by ambulance to hospital, but died the next day.

When an attempt was made to lift by crane the ends of 2 of 9 bundles of reinforcing bar (estimated 13 to 16 t) brought onto the rooftop floor for rebar placement work by about 30 cm, a particular square pipe on which the rebar had been temporarily placed bent, the other square pipes then bent in a chain reaction, and the deck plate in contact with the bent square pipes could not bear the load and collapsed as though the floor had given way. One victim who was nearby was caught up in it and fell about 11 m together with the rebar and other materials.

While cleaning windows on the south side of the third floor of an elementary school building, the victim fell about 7.7 m and struck a concrete surface. Fall arrest equipment meeting the required performance was not used.

At a site in a national forest, when a coworker felled a Japanese cedar (length 22.69 m, diameter at breast height about 30 cm) with a chainsaw, it fell about 45 degrees off the felling direction. The victim was where the cedar fell; the felled tree struck the victim around the head and back, and the victim's neck area was then pinned between the cedar and the ground.

To resolve a malfunction of an electrostatic precipitator, workers were scraping off sodium sulfate powder (hereinafter 'the powder') adhering to the walls and other surfaces inside the precipitator, when a large amount of the powder collapsed and buried three workers; one of them died and two suffered burns. The powder was about 50°C at the surface and about 80°C inside. In addition, another worker suffered burns during the rescue of the victims.

During installation work for optical communication cable, the victim was attempting to move an aerial work platform to a designated position on a slope. When the victim left the driver's seat for some reason, the aerial work platform started moving. When the victim tried to stop the moving aerial work platform by holding it with their hands, the victim was caught between it and another aerial work platform set up nearby.

The victim was performing newspaper delivery work at the above-mentioned accident location and was found lying collapsed on a stair landing of an apartment building by a resident of the building. The victim was transported by ambulance and received medical treatment, but death was confirmed. At the time of ambulance transport, the victim's body temperature was 41.7 degrees.
While operating a forklift on the premises, the victim died of acute heart failure.
After a helicopter sightseeing flight had ended, the helicopter, carrying two people, the pilot and a mechanic, crashed onto farmland while returning to the airport.
After a helicopter sightseeing flight had ended, the helicopter, carrying two people, the pilot and a mechanic, crashed onto farmland while returning to the airport.

At a crushed-stone stockyard owned by a business partner, to spray water on limestone loaded on a dump truck, a stepladder was set up leaning against the dump truck, and the victim was spraying water from the 5th step (1.4 m above the ground). When stepping up to the 6th step, the victim missed their footing, fell, and struck the back of the head hard. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet at the time.

The victim was driving an 8 t truck loaded with soil and was found with the truck overturned on a sharp downhill curve of a national highway with one lane in each direction. The victim was transported to hospital by doctor helicopter but subsequently died of hemorrhagic shock.

The victim was using an air blower to blow away debris that accumulates inside a compression molding machine called a baler (a machine that compresses and forms waste paper, cardboard, PET bottles, etc.). The safety cover had been removed. Another coworker was running the machine from the control panel; when the coworker turned off the power for the lunch break and was about to return to the office, the coworker found the victim with part of their body inside the machine. The victim had been caught between the main frame and the movable frame, and death from cervical spine injury was confirmed.

During route delivery, the victim fell while climbing the stairs of the building where a delivery destination business was located. The victim was found lying on the stairs by a passerby and transported to hospital, but subsequently died.

The victim was riding a small lawn mower, mowing turf alone on a golf course, when stung on the right thigh by a bee or wasp. After reporting to the person in charge, the victim drove a car to their regular clinic, but their condition suddenly worsened; the victim was taken by ambulance to a general hospital but died the same day of anaphylactic shock.

The victim, a newspaper deliverer, was riding a motorbike (50 cc) following a lead rider as part of newspaper delivery training, when the victim fell together with the motorbike down an embankment (depth about 5 m) below the right side of a municipal road.
While removing traffic restrictions for common utility duct construction work for electric cables on a national highway, the victim was struck by an oncoming large vehicle and died.
While driving a truck in the second travel lane of a three-lane expressway, the driver failed to notice traffic congestion ahead and collided with a vehicle. The truck driver died.
While driving a large dump truck loaded with crushed stone on a levee road, the victim ran off the road, overturned on the slope of the levee road, and fell below the levee road.

At a road improvement construction site, the principal contractor had given notice that the construction work itself on the day of the accident was cancelled because of heavy rain since the previous day. Before leaving the site, equipment used the previous day was being tidied up on top of a retaining wall at the toe of the slope, when earth and sand collapsed from the slope and one worker was swept into the river below the retaining wall. A body found in the river that this river joins was confirmed to be that worker.

An empty dump truck (a cargo vehicle with a maximum load capacity of 8.9 t, driven by the victim, with no passengers) was traveling on a prefectural road with one lane in each direction toward the shipper's construction site when, partway through a gentle right curve on a slight downhill grade, it left the road on the left side, struck the guardrail on the left side of the road and trees off the road, and came to a stop.

The victim manually removed clogged waste from a bulky-waste pretreatment device in a bulky-waste processing facility using a crowbar and other tools, and then, while taking a break in their own car parked in the parking lot, died in the car.

The victim was engaged in delivering parcels sorted at the sales office to various locations. On the day of the accident, after delivering a parcel to the last scheduled delivery destination, the victim fell from the stairs (second-floor section) of the apartment building of that last destination and died from striking the head hard.

While the victim was loading PET bottles into a packer truck (garbage compactor truck) using a forklift fitted with a bucket, for some reason the victim's entire body was caught in the rotating plate.

During belt replacement work on a belt conveyor, while a rolled belt (weight 4 t, width 90 cm) suspended by a mobile crane was being drawn onto the conveyor, the rolled belt fell from a height of about 1.5 m. One victim who was watching the work from the conveyor walkway was caught between the walkway and the belt, and another victim was struck by the belt and thrown. The victim caught between the walkway and the belt died.

To carry out earth and sand with a hand-pushed rough-terrain carrier, the victim was going down backward on a 25-degree ramp built of single scaffold tubes and boards over stone steps, when the victim's foot went into a gap of about 15 cm between boards and the victim fell; the rough-terrain carrier slid down and ran over the victim, pinning the victim from the feet to the neck.

While picking products on the first floor of a warehouse, the victim suddenly fell, then had convulsions and lost consciousness. The victim was transported to hospital, but death from heatstroke was confirmed the next day.

The victim was operating a combined roller (hereinafter 'the compaction machine') at a leveling site in a productive green land area, compacting the ground while driving the vehicle forward, when the compaction machine fell together with the victim from a slope about 1.8 m high onto the adjacent land; the victim, who was operating it, was caught by the head between the ground and the vehicle and died.

The victim began surveying work on a road alongside a river and suddenly felt ill, was taken back to the company in a company car and given fluids and other care, and an ambulance was requested; the victim was transported to hospital by ambulance but died. On the day of onset, precipitation was 0 mm and the temperature was 33.4°C (maximum temperature 35.7°C).
While driving a standard-sized cargo vehicle (4 t), the victim collided with a large truck parked on the right side of the passageway in a parking area.

At a construction site for a new university hospital building, the victim, who was the foreman for sealing work on the pedestrian deck, the balcony handrail section of the 3rd floor of the outpatient building, and the roof of the clinical building, became unwell and was then transported to hospital by ambulance, but died of acute myocardial infarction.

While mopping the treads of a staircase, the victim fell down the staircase. The staircase is used to go between the 2nd and 3rd floors of the building and has 8 steps up to the landing, 16 steps in total.

To go to a security guard work site, the victim gathered at the business premises to carpool and departed in a light four-wheeled cargo vehicle driven by a coworker. A passenger car in the oncoming lane crossed the center line and collided head-on with the light cargo vehicle in which the victim was riding. The victim's death from cerebral contusion and cerebral hemorrhage was confirmed.

At a tree-felling site in a mountain forest, while transporting dozens of logs with a forwarder, the victim failed to make a curve on the forest road, crashed into a standing tree, was thrown out, and fell into a stream 6 m below. Because the victim could not be seen, a coworker searched and found the victim lying face down and unconscious in the stream 6 m below the forest road.

The victim, a dispatched worker, was punching metal sheets using a turret punch press. A malfunction occurred in which the metal sheet was not clamped, and while the victim was making adjustments near the table, the table started moving and the cover at the end of the carriage struck the victim's face at the right temple. About 2 hours after the accident, a coworker found the victim and called an ambulance. Death was confirmed on the spot by the ambulance crew.

After the victim and a worker of the shipping source loaded building materials onto a 10 t truck, the victim alone was securing the loaded materials, and was found collapsed and unconscious on top of the load on the truck bed. The victim was then transported to hospital but died. The cause of death was multiple organ failure due to heatstroke.
During work to move steel road plates with an excavating machine, the excavating machine overturned for some reason, and the machine's assistant was trapped underneath and died.

On the day of the accident, the victim was maintaining a green alone using a soil-injection (drenching) machine. Because the victim did not return to the office by the end of working hours, workers belonging to the same department searched the premises and found that the victim had slid off the cart path (about 2 m wide) and down about 6 m together with the machine. When found, the victim was conscious and was transported to hospital, but death was confirmed the same day.
While mowing grass, the victim was stung on the left upper arm by a bee or wasp and died from the sting.

For steel utility pole connection work, the victim had climbed the pole and was supporting a metal pole section being lifted by a mobile crane, when the tip of the mobile crane's jib came into contact with an overhead high-voltage line, and the victim was electrocuted.

During work to open a pipe joint of a heat exchanger and replace a gasket, light oil (diesel) at about 200°C spurted from the primary (supply) side, injuring six people working nearby, one of whom died in the hospital where they had been admitted.

The victim, who was doing replacement work at a factory, felt unwell partway through and rested in an air-conditioned car. After contacting the company to report heatstroke symptoms, the victim drove back to the company, lost consciousness while resting in the air-conditioned car, and was taken to hospital as an emergency, but died.

At a materials storage area on the business premises, a worker who was sorting materials fell from a wooden staircase used to move from the first floor to the second floor; the worker was unconscious and subsequently died.

At a night construction site, while the victim was guiding a dump truck that had entered to deliver materials, at a cliff with no guardrail, the victim fell from the cliff to an estimated 70 to 80 m below.

The victim was pruning azaleas planted at the top of a wall in the courtyard of an apartment building, the accident site, and fell into the courtyard. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet or fall arrest equipment at the time of the fall. The victim subsequently died.

On receiving a report at the workplace that a member of the public had fallen into a dam together with their car, the victim rushed to the scene and entered the dam reservoir to rescue them. Having entered the reservoir, the victim stayed in the water, but after a while began swimming toward the shallows on the opposite bank, disappeared from view, and was later found dead on the bank of a downstream river about 5 km from the scene.

At a supplier's premises, several people were packing scrapped vehicles and automobile parts into export containers using forklifts and other equipment, when the victim was found with an injury to the side of the head from an unknown cause, and death was confirmed.

The victim entered the hoistway of a vertical conveyor installed to carry hand towels (oshibori) from the first floor to the second floor and was removing hand towels that had fallen into the hoistway, when the conveyor's car descended and the victim was caught between the car and the floor.

In the factory where the accident occurred, while the victim was using a woodworking circular saw bench to rip-cut exterior wall base material lengthwise, the material kicked back and struck the victim.
At a construction site, while the victim was clearing away materials, the victim collapsed from heatstroke and died after being transported to hospital.

To remove oil from a sunken gut ship (grab-crane cargo vessel), divers working in pairs were performing underwater oxy-arc cutting to make a 1 m x 1 m opening in the shell plating (thickness about 10 mm) of the sunken vessel as an access point to the crane post holding the oil, when a sudden explosion occurred. The worker who was assisting, including changing the cutting rods, died at the medical facility to which they were transported.

The victim, together with three workers of the principal contractor, slung steel sheet piles (in sets of three) on a truck bed with two wire ropes and was lifting them with an excavator (backhoe) equipped for mobile crane use and lowering them to the ground. While the victim was holding the end of the lifted steel sheet piles to keep the load from swinging, a principal contractor's worker swung the excavator, whereupon the wire ropes shifted, the steel sheet piles that had been suspended horizontally tilted, and they struck the victim's head.

The victim supervised an on-site maintenance contractor and also performed simple maintenance personally. After replacing a deteriorated steam-system valve in a building adjacent to a hot stove, when the victim went outdoors, the victim inhaled blast furnace gas containing a large amount of CO, discharged from an exhaust outlet at the top of the hot stove during a pre-ignition purge of the stove, developed CO poisoning, lost consciousness, and died.

In the reel inspection room, the victim was inspecting purchased paper products with an inspection machine for contamination by foreign matter. For some reason, the victim was caught by the rotating shaft of the roll on the winding side, which kept rotating with the victim's body caught in it.

To paint piping above a dissolving tank from a scaffold, the victim, instead of using the ladder attached to the scaffold, attempted to transfer onto the scaffold by climbing over the handrail of the inspection stage attached to the dissolving tank. After climbing over the handrail, the victim stepped through the lid of a receiving tank around the dissolving tank on which they had landed, and fell into the receiving tank. Because the receiving tank contained salt water at about 65 degrees, the victim suffered burns to the whole body below the neck. The victim was then hospitalized and treated but died.

The victim and two coworkers were working on a forest road, mowing grass and doing other tasks. The two coworkers were responsible for the upper and middle sections of the forest road and the victim for the lower section, each working separately, when the coworker in charge of the middle section found the victim lying on tree branches spread out beside a light truck. The victim was rushed to hospital but died the next day of acute subdural hematoma.

The victim was alone performing the monthly periodic inspection of a direct-acting hydraulic passenger elevator (rated load 0.6 t) installed in a store. The victim entered the 30 cm deep pit through the inspection door on the first floor and was soaking up oil that had leaked into the pit with absorbent sheets, when the car descended and the victim was caught between the car and the pit floor.

During repair work on a perforated hopper at the bottom of a silo and on the installation of a vibration device, in the aggregate production process for precast prestressed concrete products and similar items, a belt conveyor that had stopped after detecting an abnormality suddenly restarted because its power had not been shut off, and a worker who was working standing on the belt conveyor was caught between the roller section of the belt conveyor and the bottom of the hopper.

While the outriggers of an aerial work platform were being extended in an underground ramp, the aerial work platform began to move backward, and the victim, who was behind it, was caught; the victim was immediately transported to hospital, where death was confirmed.

At an outdoor work area on the business premises, the victim had inserted the forks of a forklift into a 'bakkan' (a metal industrial waste container), raised it to about 3.75 m above the ground, and was reversing with the center of gravity high, when the vehicle lost its balance and overturned onto its left side; the victim was thrown from the driver's seat by the impact and was caught between the head guard and the ground.

In the second-floor granule work area of a granule factory, the victim was lowering production machinery parts to the first floor using a device that raises and lowers an iron car suspended from an electric hoist along guide rails, and was found face down with the head caught between the upper frame on the door side of the car and the second-floor floor surface.

The victim went around to the rear of a work vehicle equipped with a tail gate lifter to take out a safety helmet and other items. Subsequently, a worker at the site found the victim caught between the rear door frame and the gate (platform); the victim was transported to a medical facility but died the same day.

While doing pre-treatment work on gowns in a linen supply factory, the victim felt unwell, and as heatstroke was suspected, the victim was given ice packs and an oral rehydration drink and lay down. Although clearly conscious, the victim had pain around the pit of the stomach and had difficulty taking fluids, so the victim was transported to hospital. On examination, the victim was diagnosed with dehydration and low blood pressure and admitted, but died the next morning of acute myocardial infarction caused by heatstroke.
The victim was weeding and doing other tasks in a field where green onions were grown. After finishing work, the victim felt unwell and was transported to hospital, but died.
While performing traffic control as a security guard at a sidewalk installation construction site, the victim was struck from behind by a passing vehicle (light four-wheeled passenger car).

At this site, the victim was doing rebar pressure welding work as an assistant. When the victim had difficulty walking, workers of this business took the victim to the rest area, and the victim was taken by ambulance and treated, but died the same day at the receiving hospital.

A technical intern trainee working at a lotus root farm had been placed on the bed of a light truck driven by the employer to hold down the cargo; while the truck was traveling, the trainee was thrown off on a curve, fell onto the road surface, struck the head hard, and died.

During retaining wall renovation work at a school, two workers developed heatstroke symptoms while pouring a concrete slab in the schoolyard. One recovered, but the other had convulsions and was transported to hospital. After treatment at the hospital was completed and the worker returned home, the symptoms worsened again and the worker was transported to another hospital, but died that night.

After finishing training a racehorse on the practice track inside the main track of a racecourse, while the victim was returning to the stables through the main track, the racehorse suddenly began to gallop. It galloped toward a steel practice starting gate installed about 200 m ahead, and when the horse turned to the right just before the starting gate, the victim was thrown from the horse and struck the starting gate.

On the first day of sheet waterproofing work on a building roof, after the work was finished, the victim went back up to the roof because they had forgotten something. When the victim did not come back for some time, the business owner telephoned, and the victim replied, 'I'm coming down now.' When the victim still did not come back, the owner went to get the victim and found the victim unconscious, leaning against the handrail on the second level of the scaffold.

The victim and a crane operator were loading cargo onto a truck bed. On the truck bed, the victim unhooked one side of the sling that had been used to rig the loaded cargo from the lifting chain, leaving the sling hanging from the hook. When the crane operator hoisted the hook to pull the sling out from under the load, the sling caught on the load and the cargo collapsed. The victim was struck by the collapsing load and died.

The victim stopped a truck with a maximum load capacity of 2.2 t, equipped with a tail gate lifter, in front of the shipper's premises and, together with an employee of the shipper, loaded a roasting machine (about 70 cm wide, about 100 cm deep, about 190 cm high, weighing about 400 kg, with wheels on the bottom for moving) onto the tail gate lifter. When the lifter had been raised about 50 cm, the roasting machine fell to the ground, and the victim, who was at the spot where it fell, was trapped underneath it and died.
The victim suddenly collapsed while working in the factory at the workplace and was taken by ambulance. Death was confirmed the next day at the hospital to which the victim was transported.

On a line for quenching and tempering steel wire, the steel wire being fed broke, and the victim was reconnecting the broken wire. For some reason the end of the steel wire sprang up and cut the victim's neck. The victim alerted a coworker with a call button and was then taken to hospital by ambulance, but died.

The victim was driving a 2-ton truck on an expressway. While stopped at the end of a line of vehicles because of a traffic jam, a large truck struck the victim's truck from behind, pushing it into another large truck stopped ahead in a chain-reaction collision. The victim was then taken to hospital, where death was confirmed.

The victim, who had been working alone on maintenance and inspection inside a manhole from ground level, did not return to the office by the end of working hours. Employees searched and found the victim collapsed inside the manhole (about 4 m deep), and death was later confirmed.

While crossing the road on the north side of an apartment building to check a neighborhood association notice board in the park opposite the building, the victim was run over by a truck turning right.

The victim was unloading a piece of heavy machinery (a grapple) loaded on a 10-ton truck onto the road when, for some reason, it lost balance and the victim fell together with the machine down a cliff beside the road. The owner of the forestry business, who was nearby, noticed a sound like something falling, approached, and found the machine at the bottom of the cliff and the victim lying there.

At a site where the exterior walls of a building were being painted, during scaffold assembly, the victim was standing on the fourth level of the scaffold (height 7.7 m) attaching mesh sheeting to the outside of the scaffold when the victim contacted a power transmission/distribution line above and was electrocuted.

At a crossroads intersection, the victim's (the deceased worker's) light truck, traveling westward from the east, collided with a van traveling straight from the south. After being taken to hospital, the victim was confirmed dead from right hemopneumothorax. The intersection had no traffic signals, and the road on which the van was traveling had priority.

On an expressway, the truck driven by the victim crashed into the rear of a line of vehicles in a traffic jam, and the victim was confirmed dead at the hospital to which they were taken. The impact caused a chain-reaction collision involving a total of five vehicles, and three people other than the victim were seriously or slightly injured.

During tree felling, while wedges were being driven in toward the felling direction, the tree fell in a direction different from that planned, and the victim, who was where it fell, was struck from behind by the felled tree.

In work using a bridge (gantry) crane to load steel beams temporarily stored in a yard onto a truck, the beams were stacked with five in the first tier and two in the second tier. When one of the second-tier beams was lifted and traversed, the remaining one collapsed, and a worker who was beside the stacked beams was caught between it and a nearby beam and died of traumatic asphyxia.

To move the remote control of a material-transport system installed in a tunnel inside a penstock with a 45-degree gradient from the first anchor block to the second anchor block of the penstock tunnel, the victim rode on the trolley of the system and operated the winch remote control themselves, descending at a point about 30 m along the inclined shaft, when the wire rope broke, and the victim slid down together with the trolley and struck the concrete wall of the second anchor block.

At the consignor's premises, to unload a load (822 kg) fixed to a stand from a truck bed, the victim lowered the right-side gate of the truck bed, whereupon the load fell over together with the stand. The victim tried to support it, was struck by the load, fell to the ground from the impact, and was pinned under the load.

While delivering newspapers on a motorbike, the victim entered an intersection going straight and collided at right angles (crossing paths) with a light passenger car that was also entering going straight.

The victim was performing sampling work for performance testing of a facility at the construction site of a new waste treatment facility. The victim began sampling inside the facility wearing nonwoven protective clothing and a dust mask, and after finishing about one hour of waste sampling, the victim's condition worsened and their speech became slurred, so they were taken to hospital by ambulance. The same day, the victim died of heatstroke at the hospital.

The manager, deputy manager and the victim, three people in total, were cleaning the drainage gutter on the roof of a bulky waste processing building. While bagging debris from the gutter and carrying it on the roof, the victim stepped through a 6 mm thick glass window on the roof, fell 14.75 m to the floor below, and died.

In the company's factory, the victim, working alone, used a vehicle maintenance lift (Sugiyasu Bishamon two-post lift SP-2500, capacity 2.5 t) to raise a vehicle scheduled for dismantling (BMW 320D, weighing just under 2 tons) about 1.8 m. While the victim was directly under the vehicle pulling off its plastic underbody cover by hand, the vehicle suddenly fell and the victim was pinned under it, and later died of cerebral contusion.
At the factory where the accident occurred, the victim fell from a tank truck (about 3 m high) delivering cooling water.

At a renovation site for air-conditioning equipment, toilets and other facilities, two workers were removing piping near an accessible toilet and an underground pit when an explosion occurred; one died and one was seriously injured.

Inside a building on the premises of the workplace, two people were making a chinowa (a grass ring used in Shinto rituals; diameter 2.9 m, weight 180 kg, made of cogon grass with a PVC pipe core). Immediately after one worker moved the ring on the victim's instructions, the victim, who was standing on the second step from the top of a stepladder (about 1.7 m above the ground) working to detach the ring from a temporary stand to which it was fixed, fell to the ground and hit their head on the concrete floor, and later died at the medical facility to which they were taken.

Near the entrance, facing a national highway, of a pier used for hauling out soil, the victim was trying to stop a woman who had gone out into the road to protest against the work, when the victim was run over by a dump truck that started moving to turn left, and died.

The victim, who was transporting soil and rock with a dump truck, stopped the vehicle and was about to climb onto the bed when the dump truck began to run away. The victim went around in front of the runaway dump truck and tried to stop it by hand, but the victim's head was caught between the front of the victim's own dump truck and the rear of a dump truck parked ahead, and the victim died.

The victim was a diver. While performing slinging work underwater at a depth of 1 to 3 m to lift onto land steel road plates and H-beams that had fallen into the water during the previous day's work, the slinging wire rope became loosely wound around the victim's body, and communication with the tender was lost while the victim was untangling it. The tender and others pulled the victim in by the hose and lifted them onto land, but the victim was in cardiac arrest. Resuscitation was performed with an AED and other means while an ambulance was called, and the victim was taken to hospital, where death was confirmed. The communication equipment was functioning normally.
While repairing the roof of a garage for dump trucks, the victim stepped through the corrugated slate roofing and fell about 5 m.
A large tractor-trailer truck transporting wood chips to the workplace left the road on a downhill curve and overturned (ending upside down), and the driver died.

In repair work on a faulty switch, in preparation for stopping a step-up transformer on a distribution pole, two work vehicles were parked in a line on a national highway with two lanes in each direction, and the victim was placing rubber cones around the work vehicles. A 2-ton truck approaching from behind did not follow the security guard's directions and struck the parked work vehicles and the victim; the lanyard of the victim's fall arrest equipment then caught on the handle of the cargo door on the left side of the truck, and the victim was dragged about 40 m. The victim died at the hospital to which they were taken.

During house demolition, to fell a standing tree with a diameter at breast height of 20 cm or more, the upper part of the tree was slung with a belt sling attached to the main hook of a mobile crane, and with the victim riding in a basket suspended from the auxiliary hook, the victim cut the tree with a chainsaw. The cut-off section of the tree fell and struck the victim.

The victim, a cleaning worker, was driving a light vehicle on a city road on the way to work when the vehicle crossed the center line and collided with a passenger car in the oncoming lane, and the victim died of hemorrhagic shock.

The victim, who was working alone operating a shovel loader to feed calcium carbonate into a hopper, was found collapsed in front of the left front wheel of the stopped shovel loader. In front of the hopper was an upward-sloping ramp, and the shovel loader had its shovel raised, its gear in neutral, and its parking brake not applied.

After a work boarding gangway about 25 m long was installed with a high-legged jib crane on the side of a ship under repair moored at a pier in the shipyard, while work such as unhooking the lifting wire ropes was under way, the gangway lost balance and fell. Three workers who were unhooking the wire ropes on the gangway and one representative of a marine equipment company who was about to disembark fell together with the gangway, and one of the workers doing the unhooking died.

During tree felling, the chainsaw bar became pinched in the tree being felled. When the victim pulled the chainsaw out, the chainsaw bar struck the victim's right ear, injuring it and causing bleeding. It is presumed that the victim then fell and struck their chest hard on a stump.

After arriving at the head office factory premises from the victim's own workplace, the victim was pulling an empty plastic tank toward the rear of the bed of a 4-ton truck to unload it when the victim fell backward from the truck bed to the ground. The victim died at the medical facility to which they were taken.
During pipe-laying work, while spreading and leveling bedding sand in an excavated trench about 1.8 m deep, the side wall collapsed and a mass of soil struck the victim, who died.

To cut a television service line located high up, the victim leaned a portable ladder against a wire strung more than 6 m above the ground, climbed to about 4 m above the ground, and, using a ladder rung as a footing, was cutting the service line in a standing position when the victim lost balance and fell to the ground.

A worker who had gone alone to survey the area around the accident site to prepare a construction cost estimate did not return. The workplace searched and found the victim collapsed in a forest, and death was later confirmed. Based on the injuries, the victim appears to have been attacked by a bear.
The victim, a truck driver, arrived at a port after making a delivery and parked the truck along the quay. The next morning, the victim was found drowned, floating on the surface of the sea.

As part of renovation of a traditional storehouse (dozo), to investigate repair points in the earthen wall from which rice husks used as insulation were leaking, the victim was standing on the second step of a stepladder (170 cm above the ground) removing the galvanized sheet metal of the exterior wall. Although a coworker was holding the stepladder, the victim lost balance during the work, fell, and struck their back and the back of their head hard. The victim was unconscious and was taken to hospital by ambulance, but died the same day.

During dismantling of a cable crane (lifting capacity 4.1 t), a metal mast 9 m high and weighing 5.4 t was supported by four temporary wires and two chain blocks. After one wire on the north side was removed and the tension of one wire on the east side was loosened, the mast fell and struck the head of the victim, who was walking nearby.

The victim was cutting with a chainsaw near the base of a dead tree (about 19 m tall, diameter at breast height 59 cm) that was leaning against a standing tree, in order to fell it, when the weight of the dead tree caused the chainsaw to become pinched in the cut. When the chainsaw was pulled out, the dead tree dropped off the stump and hit the ground; the impact and the springiness of the standing tree caused the dead tree's trunk to break and fall, striking the victim's head.

Powdered cement manufactured by the company was being delivered with a pneumatic bulk powder transport vehicle (maximum load 12,500 kg). To begin feeding it into a silo at the delivery site, compressed air was being sent into the vehicle's tank to pressurize it when the tank burst, and the shell plate, which opened outward from the top of the tank in the rupture, struck the victim, who was working on the left side of the vehicle.

During erection work, the victim was walking along a beam (about 12 cm wide) toward a purlin member (about 12 cm by 12 cm in cross-section and about 400 cm long) temporarily placed on the beams, in order to carry it, when the victim lost balance and fell about 3.4 m onto the concrete floor slab below. After the accident the victim was hospitalized and treated but died of cerebral contusion. The victim had been wearing a safety helmet.

While the victim was processing timber with a moulder in the sawmill building in the factory, a dust collector duct suspended by wire ropes and other means from the upper steel frame of the factory fell from a height of about 4.5 m onto the victim's head, and the victim died.

About 700 m before an expressway junction, the vehicle skidded because the road surface was wet from rain and collided with a guardrail. The victim, who was in the rear seat, was thrown out of the vehicle and died of cerebral contusion.

Using a bridge (gantry) crane (operated by the victim; lifting capacity 5.07 t), an H-beam (width 35 cm, length 718 cm, height 110 cm, weight about 2.3 t) slung with lifting clamps (at two opposing points) was moved to its designated position. The victim removed one clamp, and while the partner worker had not yet fully removed the other clamp, the victim pressed the hoist button, causing the H-beam to fall toward the victim. The victim's chest and other parts were caught by the H-beam, and the victim died.

At the accident site, the driver of a tour bus and the victim (a bus guide) were trying to pull the bus up alongside the city road at the entrance of a ryokan (Japanese inn) to prepare for departure. While the driver was reversing the bus and the victim was guiding it, the victim was caught between the bus and a utility pole behind the bus.

At the former site of a supermarket, a crack was found about 50 cm from the base of a private utility pole, so the business owner and two workers began removing it. The victim worker had climbed the pole (about 10 m high) to attach, near its top, a wire for pulling the pole down with heavy machinery, when the pole broke at the cracked section. The victim, whose lifeline was attached to the pole, fell together with the pole from about 6 m above the ground and struck the ground, hitting their head hard. The victim was taken to hospital and later died.

When a Japanese cedar with a diameter at breast height of about 40 cm and a height of about 27 m was felled, the felled tree bounced about 3.5 m in the direction opposite to the felling direction and struck the chest of the victim, who was about 3 m behind it. The workers signaled by radio, and the other workers had taken refuge behind standing trees some distance away, but because the victim had been driving wedges into the tree being felled, the victim was the last to take refuge. The victim was found collapsed in the shadow of another standing tree, and it appears that the area behind that tree was the refuge location.

At a forest thinning site, when the victim made the back cut with a chainsaw in a cedar about 20 m tall entangled with wisteria vines, the cedar split lengthwise. The victim was pinned under the split-off section of the cedar, was taken to hospital by ambulance, and died of respiratory failure due to traumatic pneumothorax.

At a demolition site, during ground-level demolition with heavy machinery, demolition debris fell and sent flying a pipe that was on the ground, and the pipe apparently struck the chest area of the victim, who was spraying water behind the machine. The victim remained unconscious, was taken to hospital, and died.

A driver for a bus company contracted to transport students used waiting time between runs to climb a tree in the school parking lot whose branches had been getting in the way, and was cutting branches with a saw when the driver fell about 3.7 m to the ground and hit their head hard. Death was later confirmed at the hospital to which the driver was taken.

On a forestry road about 3.9 m wide, a worker operating a road roller fell from the road shoulder down a slope about 20 m. At the time, the victim was a worker of a second-tier subcontractor and was operating the roller while on the way to the work location with workers of the first-tier subcontractor when it fell.

The victim was on a business trip to inspect and maintain monitoring equipment, including cameras, installed at the top of a dam gate. The victim dropped a company smartphone into the dam, and while walking in the area downstream of the dam to look for it, fell and was swept away.
The victim, who was directing following traffic behind a rotary snowplow fitted with a weeding attachment, was run over by a passenger car coming straight on.

While walking along a corridor in an office on a round of courtesy visits, the victim fell forward and struck their head hard, and because the victim developed paralysis in all four limbs, they were taken to a medical facility by ambulance. The victim was then diagnosed with cervical spinal cord injury and was hospitalized for treatment, but died of acute pulmonary embolism.

The victim was driving a forklift and, having finished carrying sawdust in a container to the second floor of the factory, reversed, but reversed too far and fell with the forklift down a slope (about 3.2 m high) into a field below. The victim, who was driving, was thrown out and pinned under the forklift. Normally the sequence is: (1) the forklift reverses, then (2) turns and returns to its original position while reversing. At the time of the accident: (1) the forklift reversed, then (3) continued reversing down the slope, and (4) fell with the forklift into the field below the slope.

While a steel rack 6 m wide, 3.5 m high and 4 m deep in a factory was being dismantled, an intermediate post of the rack (weighing 500 kg) fell toward the victim and struck the victim directly on the head.

The victim was using a wire brush to clean (prepare the surface of) a steel column member 2.6 m high, 1.6 m wide, 0.25 m deep and weighing 0.7 t at a point about 2 m high, while holding onto the column to support their body. The column the victim was working on fell so that the victim was caught between it and another steel column behind the victim, and the victim died of liver injury due to chest compression.

In a rice and wheat storage facility, while the victim was cleaning rice husks accumulated on equipment with an air hose, the victim fell about 5.6 m into a storage tank from a section without handrails on the temporary walkway leading from the aisle beside the storage tanks to a belt conveyor. The victim's safety helmet had come off and the victim was bleeding from the head. The hose the victim had been holding was hanging into the tank.

On the workplace premises, while the victim and a supervisor were carrying a refrigerator (weighing 40 kg) by the stairs from the first floor to the employee break room on the second floor, the victim, facing backward, fell to the first floor when lifting the refrigerator on the stair landing. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance and hospitalized, but later died. (The refrigerator was carried bare-handed, and the victim was not wearing a safety helmet.) Refrigerator dimensions: width 48 cm, depth 59 cm, height 126 cm.
While driving a truck on the way to a consignor's premises, the victim collided with an expressway bridge pier in the median strip.

When work began at a materials yard loading formwork shoring panels onto a truck, the victim shouted, "I've been stung by a bee." Two people nearby ran to the victim and found the victim collapsed. Because the victim was in cardiac arrest, firefighters performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but the victim did not regain consciousness; the victim was taken to hospital and admitted, and death was confirmed in the hospital.

The victim, who was on a business trip at the accident site to install new dust removal equipment, was trying to connect the dust removal equipment's wiring to a power panel (200 V) in the transformer room when the victim's body contacted a copper busbar connected to the power panel, and the victim was electrocuted and died. At the time of the accident, the power panel was de-energized, but the busbar connected to it was live.

While directing traffic under alternating one-lane traffic control, the victim confirmed that the last vehicle in the opposing lane had passed, let one waiting vehicle proceed, and was moving to their post when the victim was struck by a light truck coming forward from a side road, and later died.

On the day of the accident, the victim was weeding with a brush cutter on a slope above a stone wall along a road in a botanical garden. After the lunch break, the victim talked with a member of the public who was walking along the road below the stone wall, and was later found collapsed beside the stone wall on the road, holding the brush cutter. The height from near where the victim was lying to the slope was 3.9 m.
While a concrete stormwater pipe buried in a sports ground was being cut with an engine cutter, the engine cutter kicked back and its blade contacted the right side of the user's neck.

On the day of the accident, the victim, who was engaged in cleaning work, was found collapsed and bleeding from the head on the stair landing between the first and second floors. The victim was unconscious after the accident and died.

During tree felling on a riverbank, a felled tree became hung up on another tree. The victim began felling the tree it was hung up on, but the chainsaw became pinched in the trunk and would not move, so the victim resumed felling with a second chainsaw. When the supporting tree began to fall, the victim grabbed the pinched chainsaw and tried to escape, but the tree fell toward the victim, struck the victim in the chest, and pinned the victim underneath.

When a contractor's 2-ton truck reversed to back into the parking lot on the workplace premises, the driver did not notice the victim, and the victim was caught between the truck and a steel pole and died.

To clean an outdoor air-conditioning unit installed on the roof of a factory, the victim was walking across the roof when the victim stepped through a glass skylight and fell 7.8 m to the factory floor. At the time of the accident, the victim was not wearing a safety helmet or fall arrest equipment.

On the day of the accident, after finishing site work in the morning, the victim was driving a truck on an expressway to attend a periodic health checkup when the truck crashed into the rear of a tank truck stopped ahead.

On a business trip, while on the way to a group company of the victim's workplace, the victim was suddenly attacked from behind by an unknown person and stabbed with a bladed weapon in multiple places, including the neck and back.

Three people, including the victim, boarded a fishing boat and went offshore to set a net. After arriving at the designated location, while the net was being set from the stern, the victim disappeared from view. When the others checked from the stern, the victim's feet were entangled in the net and the victim had been dragged into the sea (about 3 m deep). The victim was pulled out about 10 minutes after falling into the sea but later died.

While the victim was collecting recyclable materials on a client's premises, the victim was struck from behind by a forklift driven by a coworker and was caught between the forklift's attachment and a building column.

The victim, driving a 10-ton truck on a national highway, crossed the center line while trying to overtake a vehicle ahead and collided head-on with an oncoming vehicle (a 10-ton truck) on a left-hand curve. Both the victim and the driver of the oncoming vehicle died. At the accident site, the victim's side of the road had one lane with a 7% downgrade, and the opposite side had two lanes including a climbing lane, for a total of three lanes.

The victim, driving a 10-ton truck on a national highway from the west, was entering a right-hand curve when an oncoming vehicle (a 10-ton truck) crossed the center line, and the right front parts of the two trucks collided (a so-called offset collision). Both the victim and the driver of the oncoming vehicle died. The victim's side of the road had a 7% upgrade, and the road had a total of three lanes including a climbing lane.

The victim, working alone on the receiving yard, was preparing to load waste near the rear of a compression-plate refuse collection vehicle (packer truck) when the victim was caught by the operating compression plate and died.

During bridge repair work, the victim and a coworker were both on the work platform of an aerial work platform vehicle. While the coworker, at the front, was raising the platform while extending the boom, the victim, who was behind the coworker, was caught between a concrete girder and the handrail of the work platform and died.

In restoration work on a village road damaged by torrential rain, the victim was breaking up an existing concrete retaining wall with a demolition machine (breaker) when the block of retaining wall being broken slid toward the valley side, and with the tip of the breaker still caught on the retaining wall, the victim fell together with the machine onto the riverbank. The victim was thrown from the machine and injured by being caught between the machine and the broken blocks of the retaining wall, and death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.
The victim collapsed at the workplace and was taken to hospital by ambulance, and later died. The direct cause of death was cerebral hemorrhage, and cerebral infarction was diagnosed.

In a forest, the victim was felling trees with the business owner to improve sunlight on a rice paddy owned by the business owner. When the business owner tried to haul out a felled tree with an excavator (backhoe), the excavator overturned, and the victim, who was nearby, was pinned underneath and died.

During river surveying, the victim, who was in a boat, was thrown into the river and was found underwater downstream. The victim was in the boat to measure the depth of the river when the victim fell out of the boat. The unmanned boat was carried away, and the victim followed it and climbed back in, but could not return to the bank and drifted, after which the boat took on water and capsized, throwing the victim into the river. The victim was wearing a life jacket. The river current was fast due to heavy rain the previous day.

At a disaster recovery construction site, the victim was operating an excavator (backhoe) with a crane function (bucket capacity 0.14 cubic meters) and carrying a wooden form suspended from it when, on a downhill slope of about 20 degrees, the excavator tipped forward, and the victim's head was caught between a head guard post of the excavator and the ground.

On the day of the accident, the victim was working alone in a warehouse, taking inner bags containing product raw materials out of cardboard cases and doing other work. A coworker found the victim walking unsteadily along an outdoor walkway outside the warehouse. The victim was then taken to hospital by ambulance but died there of traumatic cerebral hemorrhage due to a blow to the head. Shoe prints were found on the top surface of cardboard cases stacked two high (about 1 m above the floor) in the warehouse.

At a construction site for removing a utility pole, the pole broke and fell before the removal work, and the victim was pinned under it. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance and diagnosed with a dislocated right knee. While hospitalized, a blood vessel became occluded, the victim subsequently developed non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia, and then died.

In seismic reinforcement work on bridge piers, to carry out materials for temporary structures, the victim used an excavator (backhoe) with a crane function on a barge to lift a 450 kg H-beam and swung it, whereupon the victim fell into the river together with the excavator. The victim was rescued two and a half hours later, but death was confirmed at the scene.
While traveling with a wheel loader at a surplus soil disposal site, the victim fell from the road shoulder, was pinned under the wheel loader, and died.

The victim was driving a 4-ton truck on an expressway to return to the office when, near a service area, the truck crashed at high speed into the rear of the last truck in a traffic jam that was crawling along, and the victim died. The load was 1.5 t of new pallets.

In a railway station area, the victim climbed a utility pole to replace a low-voltage line (100 V) and, while repositioning a body-holding device and doing other work near the crossarm, for some reason grabbed a high-voltage line (6,600 V) about 1.2 m above the low-voltage line and was electrocuted.
