Because the low-voltage line was de-energized for the work and approaching the high-voltage line was not planned, insulating protective covers and insulating personal protective equipment were not used.

The victim was found dead by hanging in their apartment. As psychological stressors, there had been a marked change in the content and volume of work and trouble with subordinates; the overall evaluation of psychological stress was judged "strong," and the victim had developed "F32 depressive episode."

The victim was sorting PET bottles in the workplace warehouse. After a break, the work supervisor found the victim slumped forward and motionless at the work location. Because the victim did not respond when spoken to, an ambulance was called, and the victim was taken to hospital and admitted that day. Death was later confirmed. The cause of death was "multiple organ failure due to heatstroke."
The victim was found collapsed in a stall of the men's toilet at an expressway service area. A subsequent postmortem examination estimated the cause of death as acute cardiac death.

The victim was working alone operating the 5-ton hoist of an overhead travelling crane (5-ton, for tandem lifting) to place an H-beam (about 11 m long, weighing about 4 tons) on the feeder of a shot blasting machine. The crane's lifting clamp caught on the H-beam, and the victim, who was working on top of the feeder, fell with the toppling H-beam to below the feeder (about 90 cm) and was pinned under the H-beam.

While standing trees were being cut at a construction site, vines were entangled in a felled tree, and the momentum of its fall pulled on other standing trees; part of a tree that broke and flew off struck the victim directly on the head.

Work was planned to install a water spray device on a refrigeration condenser (outdoor unit) installed on the canopy of a store. The victim was making preparations on the canopy when, for some reason, the victim misstepped and fell about 4.5 m to the asphalt ground below. The victim was not wearing fall arrest equipment or a safety helmet.

To transport waste collected in house cleaning work to a disposal site, the victim was driving a medium-sized truck on an expressway when the truck crashed into the rear of a large trailer stopped in a traffic jam in the first lane. The victim was taken to a medical facility but died the same day of severe multiple trauma.

The accident occurred at a site where the roof and exterior walls of a private house were being painted. It is presumed that the victim, who was about to work on the roof over the entrance, rolled off the roof and fell straight through the gap between the handrail and the mid-rail of the scaffold set up around the roof. The eaves of the roof were about 3.4 m above the ground.

During loading of coconut shells (biomass fuel) into the hold of a cargo ship, after an excavator (backhoe) to be used in the work had been lowered into the hold, two workers opened the hatch in the hold ceiling, entered the hold to unhook the slings, and were waiting on top of the coconut shells when they lost consciousness. One regained consciousness, but the other died. At the time of the accident, about 8,000 t of coconut shells were loaded in the hold, and no work had been done the previous day.

To determine where to attach wire ropes and other equipment for pulling down a dead tree, because climbing the dead tree was dangerous, it was decided to observe the top of the dead tree from the upper part of a nearby tree. The victim climbed the nearby tree with a rope, passed a rope attached to the fall arrest equipment around a branch of that tree, and, suspended from the branch in a U-shaped (work-positioning) configuration, was moving toward the end of the branch while changing over the lifeline, when the branch broke and the victim fell together with the branch about 13.8 m to the ground.

After leaving the workplace to transport materials to a construction site, while traveling on a city road the victim's vehicle, for some reason, collided with a building at a materials yard, and the victim died of cerebral contusion.

A large truck driven by the victim broke through a guardrail beside the road, struck a tree, and overturned. The site was a straight road with three lanes in each direction and good visibility. On the day of the accident, the victim had left the workplace and loaded cargo, and was scheduled to travel by ferry to the consignor's premises.

Four workers were traveling in a commercial van on a national highway to move to a grass-cutting work site when, because the road surface was wet after rain, the tires skidded, the vehicle went out of control, and it collided with a guardrail. The impact injured three people other than the driver, and one who was sitting in the rear seat (driver's side) was thrown out of the vehicle, pinned under the overturned vehicle, and died.

A product placed on a trolley (gas-insulated switchgear for a substation, fixed to the trolley with lashing belts; product about 3.5 m high by 2.3 m wide, about 3 t) was being moved about 8 m to the test position in an airtightness test room, with the victim leading and an employee of the client company (where the victim was dispatched) pushing. After it had moved about 5 to 6 m, the product toppled together with the trolley in the direction of travel, and the victim was pinned underneath. The victim died while hospitalized with a pelvic fracture and injuries to the bladder, kidney and large intestine.

To prepare an estimate for replacing a tiled roof, the victim put a foot on the first rung of a ladder to climb onto the roof, and fell from the ladder. Immediately after the accident the victim was conscious, but later died.

To unload ordered building materials at a customer's warehouse, the victim backed the truck in and stopped, got out of the driver's seat, and was opening the warehouse shutter when the truck began to run away, and the victim, who was behind it, was caught between the truck and the building and died.

At a ryokan (Japanese inn) whose cleaning work had been contracted out, the victim, who was working alone loading futons and other items put out at the garbage area for disposal into a disposal container, was found collapsed inside the container.

While traveling from home in a company vehicle (a van) directly to a machinery installation site, the victim was stopped on an expressway when the vehicle was struck from behind by a truck. There were no passengers.

On an expressway, a large truck crashed into the rear of a line of vehicles stopped in a traffic jam, causing a chain-reaction collision involving seven vehicles. Three passenger cars were wrecked and caught fire; three people including the victim died, and three others were seriously or slightly injured. The victim was traveling home in a company vehicle (a passenger car) and was stopped at the end of the traffic jam.

During work removing sediment accumulated in a stormwater drainage ditch using a small excavator (backhoe), the engine cover of the excavator suddenly opened, and the victim, who was operating the machine from the seat on top of that cover, was thrown off backward, fell to the ground, and suffered a cervical spinal cord injury. The victim later died of aspiration pneumonia at the hospital where they were receiving treatment.

The victim set out from the office to a forestry site in a light company van to check the site before work began. Later, a passerby found the light van overturned and burning on the left-side embankment of a gentle right-hand downhill curve (gradient about 4 degrees) on a prefectural road, and after the fire was extinguished, the victim was found in the rear of the vehicle.

At a construction site for a new hospital, elevator installation work was being carried out. Inside the hoistway, scaffold boards were placed across the frame of the car to serve as a working platform, located at a height of 23 m. While the victim was doing rust-proofing and other work on the platform, some of the platform's fixing hardware came off, the platform tilted, and the victim fell to the ground. The victim was taken to hospital, where death was confirmed.

On the premises of a customer's factory, while unloading empty containers from the cargo bed of a van-type truck to the ground, the victim fell backward about 1 m from the rear of the cargo bed and struck their head hard. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet during the work. The rear of the van-type truck was equipped with an under-floor stowable tail lift, but it was stowed at the time of the accident.

The victim was carrying out water-level management and cleaning at a headworks (river intake weir). The victim's wife, concerned that the victim was late returning home, contacted the workplace; coworkers searched around the site but could not find the victim and reported it to the police. Fire department personnel searching the area found the victim on a sandbar about 2 km downstream, and death was confirmed at the scene. There were no witnesses to the accident, and a walkway plank had been placed across the fishway of the headworks.

At a gas station, to position a customer's passenger car in front of the car wash machine, a coworker was driving the car and the victim was signaling in front of it. When the coworker drove the car forward, it struck the victim. The car continued moving forward, and the victim was caught between the front of the car and a concrete wall at the back of the premises.

To clear a blockage in an agricultural drainage basin (90 cm deep), the victim was trying to connect the end of a hose for connecting to a vacuum truck to a drainpipe located about 24 cm below ground level inside the basin, and apparently fell into the basin; the victim was found with the upper body inside the basin. The victim was then taken to hospital but died of drowning.
While extending the hose for pumping out human waste (night soil) from a private house, the victim fell from the top of a retaining wall about 4 m high.

To bring a temporary gantry crane about 12 m high into a factory, an opening was temporarily made in the factory roof, about 9 m high, so that the crane would not interfere with it. On the afternoon of the day of the accident, while the victim and four others were installing plywood boards around the opening as related work, the victim stepped through an FRP skylight panel, fell, and died.

The victim was leveling soil brought from a site using an excavator (backhoe) at a materials yard owned by the prime contractor. When a coworker came to the yard to unload soil, the coworker found the victim lying unconscious between the left and right crawlers at the rear of the excavator, with the right arm pinned under a crawler. Death from multiple trauma was later confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken. When the victim was found, the excavator's engine was running.

At a T-junction without traffic signals on a national highway, the victim, riding a moped (motorized bicycle), turned left out of the side road onto the national highway and collided with a truck traveling on the highway.
For some reason, the car of a lift descended, and the victim was caught between the bottom of the car and the pit floor. The rated load of the lift was 200 kg.

In a parking lot within a facility, before departure, with the driver's door open, the victim removed the wheel chock placed at the driver's-side front wheel; because the shift lever was in drive, the vehicle moved forward and struck the facility. The victim was caught between the closing door and the vehicle body and died.

A hopper being fabricated in the factory (2.1 m high, 3.8 m wide, mass 2 t) was unbolted and split vertically into two parts. To move one part, a crane operator used an overhead travelling crane to lift the near side, then, leaving the load suspended, left the operating position, moved to the far side, and used a second overhead travelling crane to lift the far side, whereupon the suspended load swung, contacted the other part that was not being lifted, and that part contacted a worker waiting nearby, who died.

After arriving at work and parking the victim's own car in the employee parking lot, the victim fell while climbing the outdoor stairs (average gradient 44 degrees) at the factory's staff entrance, hitting their head and fracturing the right wrist. A CT scan the next day led to a diagnosis of cerebral contusion and acute subdural hematoma, and the victim underwent head surgery. Fever and difficulty breathing then developed, pneumonia due to complications was diagnosed, and the victim died of acute heart failure.

In new building construction, during work unloading beam members for the construction from the bed of a truck with a mobile crane, when a beam was lifted with the mobile crane, it contacted beams loaded beside it; as a result, those beams fell from the truck, and the driver of the truck, who was on the ground, was pinned under the fallen beams and died.

To collect an empty marine shipping container that had been unloaded, the victim drove a tractor unit and coupled it to the chassis (trailer) carrying the container. The victim then left the driver's seat and was retracting the chassis outriggers when the trailer suddenly began to move forward. The victim hurriedly went around to the front of the truck to try to stop it, but the trailer did not stop, and the victim was caught between it and another truck in the trailer's path.

The victim was found collapsed on the bed of a truck at a delivery destination due to a cerebral hemorrhage. Despite subsequent treatment, the victim became bedridden for a long period and died of acute heart failure.

At a site for the extension and renovation of a two-story wooden house, two workers were installing first-floor beam members. A coworker standing on the dirt floor handed one end of a beam member to the victim, who was standing on a beam, and then lifted a tool carrying the other end of the beam member, at which point the beam member slipped and moved; the reaction caused the victim to lose balance and fall about 3 m from the beam. The victim was wearing neither a safety helmet nor fall arrest equipment.
During demolition work on a building, the victim was fastening scaffold boards with binding wire on a scaffold when he received an electric shock from a high-voltage line near the scaffold and died.

A stand for an ice machine to be installed in a factory (steel, 4.3 m long, 2.1 m high, weighing about 900 kg) was being transported while lifted at the front with a hand lift and at the rear with a forklift. Because it could not make it around a corner inside the factory, the workers decided to transfer the stand onto a cart temporarily; when the front of the stand was taken off the hand lift and placed on the cart, the stand fell over, and the victim, who was doing the transfer work next to the stand, was pinned under it and died.

To remove tree branches caught on power lines, the victim placed a stepladder on the bed of a light truck, straddled the top plate, and knelt on the second step from the top gripping the stepladder between both legs. While trying to cut the branches with long-reach pruning shears, the victim lost balance and fell from the stepladder (2.16 m above the ground) toward the front of the light truck. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet.

While driving a car on an expressway on the way home, the worker developed "cardiac tamponade, aortic dissection" and died. Overtime and holiday work exceeding 80 hours per month was found in the six months before onset.

A group of 17 workers including the victims were trying to drop scale inside the combustion chamber of a boiler down to the bottom of the boiler from a work platform installed inside the combustion chamber when the platform collapsed, and two workers fell about 20 m to the bottom of the boiler.

A group of 17 workers including the victims were trying to drop scale inside the combustion chamber of a boiler down to the bottom of the boiler from a work platform installed inside the combustion chamber when the platform collapsed, and two workers fell about 20 m to the bottom of the boiler.

A case holding tissue boxes with printed exteriors collapsed inside the hoistway of a vertical conveyor. When the victim entered the hoistway to fix it, the victim's head was caught between the lift section and a beam surrounding the lift.

In the process of dropping sand from a storage bin into a weighing bin at a concrete plant, sand clogged the discharge outlet of the storage bin, so the victim and the victim's supervisor entered the storage bin and were removing the blockage with shovels. When the blockage cleared, the victim was swept down by the force of the sand being discharged below and was buried alive.

Inside a moored RORO ship (a cargo ship with vehicle decks), during work to couple a tractor unit to a trailer, the victim got out of the driver's seat and was connecting the air hose when the unoccupied vehicle began moving forward. The victim, who was on the right side of the vehicle, tried to get back into the driver's seat to stop it and was caught between the right side of the vehicle and the inner wall of the ship.

The victim was using a forklift to move loads brought into a work yard to various locations within the yard. After unloading, while reversing the forklift to carry the next load, the backrest, which was raised to a high position, struck an automatic sorting machine and the forklift tipped over. The victim was thrown from the forklift's driver's seat and was pinned under the forklift.

The victim loaded cargo onto a company-owned vehicle (a truck with a loader crane) and left the company. While traveling on a national highway, the vehicle driven by the victim crossed the center line and collided head-on with a large trailer traveling in the opposite direction. The driver of the oncoming vehicle was injured and hospitalized.

In the security headquarters tent at the top of a slope at the entrance to a temple, after finishing the day shift, the victim stood up from a crouching position, fell backward, and struck the back of the head hard. The victim was taken by ambulance, but death was confirmed.

During road repair work, the victim was trying to remove debris (pieces of asphalt) lying on the road after the asphalt had been stripped when a road roller reversed and its rear roller struck the victim's back, lower back, and other areas.

The victim, who was doing closing work at a store, made an emergency call saying "I have a headache and my speech is slurred," but stopped responding partway through the call. Emergency services arrived, found the victim unconscious lying face up on the floor at the back of the office in the store, and took the victim to hospital by ambulance, but the victim later died.

During cleaning and repair work on a silo storing raw material (cornstarch) for a beer factory, a worker engaged in cleaning inside the silo was caught in the discharge of the cleaned raw material and was buried alive.

At a residential land development site, the victim was driving a road roller (compaction machine) along a temporary construction road within the site to move to another compaction location. When reaching a downhill slope (gradient about 16 degrees), the left front wheel ran off the shoulder of the slope and the roller fell down a 30-degree slope about 3.5 m high (slope length 7 m). The victim, who was thrown from the road roller, was struck by the road roller, and death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was taken.
The victim was driving a tractor towing a turbine blower and blowing away cut grass with the turbine blower when the tractor overturned and the victim was pinned under the tractor.
While operating a forklift at a fishing port, the victim fell into the sea together with the forklift.

The work involved painting the exterior walls of a building using a wedge-connection type scaffold erected outside the building. While painting on the fifth level of the scaffold (about 9 m high), the victim fell over on the scaffold deck and dropped onto the deck of the fourth level (about 7.6 m high), then fell from the fourth-level deck as well, broke through the mesh sheet on the side opposite the building structure, and fell to the ground. The victim was taken to hospital unconscious, but death was confirmed.

During surface preparation (scraping) of steel members in a factory, a steel member was lifted with two clamps attached, using an overhead crane, in order to rotate it, but the steel member became unbalanced and fell. The head of the worker, who was standing near the side of the steel member operating the crane, was caught under the falling steel member and injured. The worker was immediately taken to a medical facility but died of head trauma.

The victim was going down an indoor staircase leading from the first floor to the second floor, cleaning the stairs with a handheld vacuum cleaner from the middle landing downward, when the victim fell backward to the bottom from around the eighth step above the first floor.

To carry out a geological survey of the ground, the victim was using a boring machine to insert a boring rod (115 cm above the work platform, rotating 60 to 120 times per second) into a slope in a direction parallel to the ground. To check the pressure gauge and other instruments, the victim tried to pass under the boring rod without stopping the machine, and the hood of the rain jacket the victim was wearing became entangled in the boring rod and the victim was caught in it.

While driving a truck, the victim went straight through a signalized four-way intersection on a red light, and the driver's side of the truck was struck by another vehicle coming straight from the right. When the victim steered to the left, the truck leaned to the right and crashed into a utility pole.

The victim's work was loading prepared foods, boxed meals, and other products for convenience stores at a manufacturing plant, transporting them to a distribution center, and unloading them. On the day before the accident, the victim did the above transport work, then rested for about three hours, loaded cargo again at the manufacturing plant, and departed to transport it to the distribution center. Afterward, the victim's vehicle rear-ended a vehicle ahead inside a motorway tunnel.

While traveling through a motorway tunnel, the truck driven by the victim collided with a truck that had already been in a collision and was stopped. A chain-reaction collision followed in which five following vehicles collided. Four ordinary vehicles had also been involved in collisions in front of the truck that the victim's truck hit. In the tunnel, a trailer had burned completely, and visibility was poor due to smoke from that fire.

The victim (factory manager), who was dismantling an LP gas tank truck, was injecting water into the tank through a manhole on the side of the tank when an explosion occurred inside the tank. As a result, the victim was hit by the blast that erupted from the manhole on the side of the tank and died. The victim's work clothes had been destroyed by the explosion. At the time of the explosion, two people including the victim were working, and the other worker was cutting holes in the tank using a gas cutting torch on the side of the tank.

Maintenance work on a mechanical parking facility. During an operation check in manual mode, there was an abnormal noise near the lift. When the victim looked in while the machine was running to identify the cause, the victim's head was caught between a support post of the pallet that carries vehicles and part of the equipment. When the machine was run in the reverse direction to rescue the victim, the victim was freed, but had already lost consciousness and fell into a pit about 2.5 m deep below the lift.

At the site of demolition work on a coal preparation plant, the victim was operating a demolition machine (steel frame cutter) to remove machinery and other equipment installed inside a building when, for some reason, the building being demolished collapsed and the victim was buried under it together with the heavy machine and died.

After arriving at a delivery destination from the business site, the victim lost consciousness while unloading on site. Following a call from the site, the victim was taken to hospital by emergency transport, and death was confirmed at the hospital the same day. (Diagnosis: myocardial infarction)

During exterior wall repair work on a prefectural housing complex, the victim was installing screens and sashes on windows while on a work platform projecting from the main scaffold toward the building, lost balance, and fell about 10 m to the ground through the gap between the building and the scaffold. At the time of the accident, the victim was wearing only an old-style waist-belt safety belt rather than a full-harness fall arrest device, and moreover had not attached the hook to anything.

For golf course maintenance, the victim was riding a mowing tractor along a cart path to the mowing location when, for some reason, the tractor ran off the cart path and fell down a slope (gradient about 30 degrees) leading to the 10th hole tee ground. Because the victim was not wearing a seat belt, the victim was thrown from the tractor and was found by a coworker lying about 8 m from the point of the fall.

A worker nearby found the victim caught between an agricultural tractor (walk-behind type) and the frame of a plastic greenhouse inside the greenhouse. The victim had been tilling soil inside the greenhouse alone, and when found, the agricultural tractor was in reverse gear and was continuing to move backward.

During roof renovation work on a cattle barn, while working on a roof about 6.9 m high, the victim stepped through a roof panel (Galvalume steel sheet), fell, and died. The roof panel that was stepped through was heavily rusted and fragile.
While turning right at an intersection to deliver evening newspapers, a one-box van approached from behind and rear-ended the two-wheeled vehicle the victim was riding.

After delivering ready-mixed concrete to a construction site with a concrete mixer truck, the victim stopped the mixer truck on a farm road and got out to hand a delivery slip to a site worker. The mixer truck started moving, so the victim, who was behind the vehicle, ran toward it, but the vehicle fell into a waterway on the right side of the road together with the victim. The victim's head was caught between the rear body of the vehicle and the slope where it fell, and the victim died at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

The injured worker, who had been felling Japanese cypress trees with a chainsaw, was found by a coworker pinned under a felled cypress (about 19.5 m long). Two more felled trees were piled on top of that felled tree. The worker was taken to hospital, but death was confirmed. The cause of death was traumatic asphyxia.

To repair the part that flips the aluminum plates in a large-plate paper interleaving machine (a machine that inserts paper between aluminum plates) that had malfunctioned, with the machine's power turned off, the victim removed a lock pin on the machine's air cylinder with a hammer, whereupon the air cylinder moved and the victim's head was caught by a structural part of the machine.
While making a regular patrol of a park by bicycle, the victim fell and hit the head, and was receiving medical treatment but later died.

The victim was driving a company car (light vehicle) on a national highway with one lane in each direction, returning from a client to the workplace, when the car entered the opposing lane and collided head-on with an oncoming vehicle (a large dump truck).
A worker on a break was walking within the premises at the accident location when the worker was run over by a concrete mixer truck driven by a worker from another company, and died of head trauma.

On a barge (special vessel) moored alongside a ship berthed in the harbor and collecting wastewater, the injured worker (A) and the injured worker (B), who belonged to a subcontractor, were transferring wastewater from floating matter removal tank (No. 4) to the same type of tank (No. 3) when a bag-shaped filter installed on the top cover of No. 3 fell to the bottom of the tank, which is 3.8 m high. B entered the tank to retrieve it and was affected. A noticed something was wrong with B, entered the tank to help, and was affected.

On a barge (special vessel) moored alongside a ship berthed in the harbor and collecting wastewater, the injured worker (A), who belonged to the principal contractor, and the injured worker (B) were transferring wastewater from floating matter removal tank (No. 4) to the same type of tank (No. 3) when a bag-shaped filter installed on the top cover of No. 3 fell to the bottom of the tank, which is about 3.8 m high. B entered the tank to retrieve it and was affected.

During septic tank installation work, to construct retaining walls at the septic tank installation location, concrete was placed and cured in a U shape (three sides: floor, north face, and south face; north face: 3.36 m wide, 1.6 m high, 0.4 m thick; south face: 3.36 m wide, 1.6 m high, 0.16 m thick). Afterward, the formwork was removed, and the victim entered the septic tank installation location and was shoveling out soil that had flowed in from the east and west when, for some reason, the south retaining wall fell over and the victim was caught around the chest.

The victim, who delivered feed, was refilling a 7.905 m high feed tank at a poultry farm (the delivery destination) with feed from a bulk truck, and was found by a worker of the poultry farm lying collapsed between a poultry house and the feed tank.

The victim submerged a plastic bottle containing waste liquid in a tub of water and was diluting it little by little by turning the cap slightly to create a gap, when the bottle suddenly burst and the victim was splashed with the waste liquid from the head to the abdomen, suffering third-degree burns. The victim continued treatment in hospital afterward but died.

At the site of demolition work on a waste incineration facility, during work to pull out a pile (concrete pile) buried in the ground, the upper part of the pile being pulled out broke off and fell, striking the victim directly.

While cleaning windows of a four-story building using rope access work at height, the main rope and lifeline, which had been fastened to a member of the rooftop structure, came loose, and the victim fell from a height of about 13 m to the ground.

The victim was driving a feeding truck with an integrated cattle feed mixer and was engaged in feeding cattle. Another worker, finding it suspicious that the truck had been stopped for several minutes with the auger screw in the mixer still running, climbed onto the truck's step to check inside the mixer and found the victim dead, caught in the auger screw. The step is about 1.6 m above the ground, and the mixer is about 2.4 m above the ground.

To transport processed Japanese cedar logs on a truck (flatbed truck, maximum load capacity 12.1 t), the victim and one worker of a primary subcontractor were loading logs using a forwarder and a processor, respectively, when a cedar log being loaded (weighing about 270 kg, 3.82 m long, butt-end diameter 38 cm, top-end diameter about 24 cm) fell toward the victim's side and injured the victim.

The victim was operating a feller buncher to yard logs felled on a slope when, for some reason, a log struck the protective guard of the operator's cab and penetrated it, and the victim was caught between the log and the operator's seat and died. No tree felling was being carried out at the time of the accident, and there was no work being done at different elevations simultaneously.

The victim was loading packing materials onto a goods lift in the second-floor warehouse of a factory to send them down to the first-floor factory. A coworker who found it suspicious that the victim had not come back to the first floor checked the second-floor warehouse and found the victim with the upper body caught between the lift and the second-floor floor surface.
In the travel lane inside a motorway tunnel, the vehicle driven by the victim rear-ended the back of a truck that had stopped due to a separate accident.

At a machine called a spinning machine, which tapers steel pipes (into a conical shape), the victim, who was doing adjustment work and other tasks (at the part of the machine called the drawing roll stand, was caught behind both knees between the headstock line, which had returned to its home position, and the drawing roll stand, and both legs were severed, and the victim died.

Two workers who cleaned buildings at night were riding in a light vehicle to travel between cleaning locations. When they tried to turn right at an intersection on a national highway with two lanes in each direction, they collided with a passenger car going straight, and the driver and the passenger of the light vehicle were both injured and taken to a medical facility; the passenger died the same day of multiple trauma and other injuries.

To repair the roof (slate-covered) of a factory, the victim climbed onto the roof alone, stepped through a skylight section of the roof (about 1.5 m square), and fell 6.2 m to the ground. The victim was being treated in hospital but died.

At a construction site, after placing ready-mixed concrete and washing off the ready-mixed concrete stuck to the mixer truck and to the bucket of an excavator (backhoe), the injured worker was caught between the bucket of the excavator (backhoe), which had swung around, and the mixer truck.

While doing plaster (shikkui) work on the roof of a house, the victim fell about 8.4 m from near the corner of the north side of the roof onto the premises of the neighboring house. A wedge-connection type scaffold had been erected around the house, and the roof perimeter was enclosed by the scaffold handrails. On the north side of the roof, where the victim fell, the scaffold work platform had been installed below the eaves, but there was no work platform around the roof.

During levee reinforcement work, the victim had been standing beside an excavator (backhoe) to prepare for excavating soil from the levee slope and loading it onto the bed of a 2 t truck, but moved between the 2 t truck, which was reversing, and the bucket of the excavator, and the victim's chest was caught between the bucket of the stopped excavator and the reversing 2 t truck, causing injuries including tracheal rupture. The victim was then taken to hospital but died of hypoxic encephalopathy.

A fabricated steel beam for a high-rise building (about 12.3 m long, about 1.44 m high, weighing 4.4 t) had been loaded onto the bed of a trailer truck using a gantry crane, and the victim was removing the lifting gear on the bed and preparing to secure the beam to the bed when the beam fell toward the victim. The victim jumped down to the ground but was pinned under the beam. Death was confirmed at the hospital.

The victim was changing the tires of a 5-ton truck from winter tires to normal tires in the building with the business site's parking area. After removing the front wheel on the driver's side, the victim went under the vehicle body for some reason, whereupon the jack supporting the front of the vehicle body came off and the victim was pinned under the vehicle body and died.

While on the way by bicycle from home to the nearest station, the victim came into contact with a car driven by another party, and death was confirmed the same day. On that day, the victim had the traffic accident while on the way to a work location different from the office where the victim usually worked.
On a frontage road of a national highway, a truck coming from behind rear-ended a large trailer stopped on the road shoulder. The driver of the truck that rear-ended the trailer died.
A felled tree (Japanese cedar) about 30 m tall struck the victim, who had entered a cedar felling site to photograph the work.
While cleaning a udon noodle-making machine (mixer), the victim's head was caught between the rotating tank and a steel plate cover.

At a road disaster recovery work site, an excavator (backhoe) stopped on the road surface was being used to lift a mokko (rope net carrier) filled with cobblestones and lower it about 3.7 m below the road. When the arm was moved toward the valley side, the excavator fell from the road shoulder, and the victim, who was thrown from the excavator, was caught between a standing tree and the arm, was taken by ambulance, and died.

The victim, a slinger, was carrying out timber while communicating by radio with the operator of a yarder when the load-hoisting rope of the yarder broke, and the timber being carried or the severed load-hoisting rope struck the victim. The victim was taken to hospital but died. The people on site that day were three: the deceased victim, the yarder operator, and the site supervisor.

At a business that collects and sells metal, the business owner was using a grapple to prepare for loading a truck in the afternoon. When the grapple was swung around, the victim's chest was caught between the rear of the upper rotating structure and nearby compacted metal scrap.
While delivering newspapers on a motorbike, the victim was turning right on a road when the victim collided with a medium-sized truck coming straight from the opposite direction and died.

A worker in the casting and melting process in a factory noticed a crushed helmet coming down the casting production line, immediately stopped the production line, and checked the work area of the preceding molding process, where the victim, who had been working in the molding process, was found dead with the head caught in a mold-making machine.

While working on the opposite bank of a river, the river rose due to heavy rain. To evacuate, the victim was crossing the river in a small boat by following a rope stretched across the river when the small boat capsized and the victim was swept away by the river.

At a quarry maintenance work site, during the felling of standing trees to create an access entrance, the victim, who had been gathering branches, was found lying near a fallen tree. The victim was taken by ambulance, but death was confirmed at the hospital.
When the victim tried to step from the side gate of a trailer dump truck's bed onto a ladder for getting down, the victim fell to the ground from a height of 2.8 m.

While dismantling a wedge-connection type scaffold erected for painting work on a private house, the injured worker was moving on the roof of the building to remove horizontal braces, slipped, slid off the roof, and fell 6.3 m to the ground.
The injured worker died by suicide in a shed at home.
At a treatment tank for microbial decomposition of livestock manure and urine, the victim fell into the tank through a manhole (65 cm in diameter) on top.

While delivering newspapers on a company-owned small motorbike, the victim was traveling along a straight road (municipal road) with no center line toward the next delivery point when the victim fell, struck the head hard, and died.

On a prefectural road, the vehicle driven by the victim crossed into the opposing lane, hit a curb on the road, and then collided head-on with an oncoming large tank truck. Death from traumatic aortic rupture was confirmed at the medical facility to which the victim was taken. At the time of the accident, the victim was traveling in a light vehicle.

Cleaning and washing of a rough terrain crane was being done by one operator and three workers. Two of the three workers washed with high-pressure washers, and one was a relief worker, with the workers rotating as appropriate. When the tires were being turned to wash the back of the tires, the victim, who was the relief worker, was standing in the gap between a tire and the machine body and was caught between the tire and the machine body.

The victim was doing CO2 arc welding work on a bulkhead in a tank of a chemical tanker under construction when welding sparks ignited something and a fire broke out inside the tank. The victim put the upper body out of the tank's manhole, told workers nearby that a fire had broken out inside the tank, and then went back into the tank. The victim was found inside the tank.

After asphalt spreading work using a 6.0 m class asphalt finisher was finished, the asphalt finisher was being moved to an off-site parking lot. When it was turning right at an intersection, because it risked contacting the sidewalk curb, the driver turned the steering the other way and reversed, and the victim, who had been spreading asphalt with a rake behind the asphalt finisher, was caught at the thighs between the rear of the asphalt finisher and a utility pole and died.

During scaffold dismantling work, with one worker posted on each level from the top level of the scaffold to the bottom level, materials from scaffolding dismantled the previous day were being passed down from top to bottom. The victim, who was working on the second level from the top, left the spot where materials were being passed for some reason, fell from the scaffold (about 10.3 m high), bounced off a protective cover on power lines, and landed face down on the ground. Two rows of handrails were installed at the location of the fall.

To relocate the outdoor lighting of a hair salon on the first floor of a three-story apartment building, the victim was moving to the work location over the 3.6 m high first-floor roof and fell. There were no fall prevention measures such as handrails on the roof, and the victim was not wearing fall arrest equipment meeting the required performance or a safety helmet. After being injured, the victim was taken to hospital, where death was later confirmed.

To remove the temporary embankment of a cofferdam on the left bank of the main river channel, the victim, working alone, had finished work on the right bank with an excavator (backhoe) and was traveling toward the downstream left bank side to cross the main river channel from the right bank to the left bank when the riverbed collapsed, and the excavator rolled over toward a deep spot in the riverbed about 3 m deep that had been scoured by the current and was submerged, and the victim drowned.
At a demolition work site, during work to remove urethane near the ceiling of a building using a high-pressure washer, the representative of the victim's employer found the workers lying collapsed.

To repair the air spring of the air suspension on the front wheel of a large truck, worker A used the remote control installed in the driver's cab to send air to the air suspension and widen the space between the tire and the vehicle body. The victim then put the upper body into the gap between the front tire on the passenger side and the vehicle body to repair the air suspension, when the vehicle body suddenly dropped and the victim's head and neck were caught between the tire and the vehicle body, and the victim died.

To unload reinforcing bar cages for cast-in-place piles stacked in two tiers on a trailer bed, the victim was loosening the chain blocks of the wires securing the cages when the load collapsed and the victim was pinned under the reinforcing bar cages and died.
The victim was working with an internal-combustion-powered forklift in a warehouse with its windows and doors closed and died of carbon monoxide poisoning.

During concrete placement into 3 m high wall formwork, the wall formwork collapsed, and a total of six workers (one of whom was the business owner) who were working on a work scaffold installed on top of the wall formwork (about 5 m high) — the concrete pump truck operator, vibrator operators, and concrete leveling workers — fell from the scaffold along with the collapsing wall formwork and were caught between the collapsed wall formwork and steel columns.

The victim was felling a standing tree (27 m tall, 38 cm diameter at breast height) with a chainsaw. When the back cut was made, the tree split vertically, perpendicular to the ground, and the split tree struck the victim directly and pinned the victim underneath; the victim went into cardiopulmonary arrest and later died.

The victim was painting on the second-floor roof of the site building when the victim fell 4.2 m from the eaves of that roof onto a polycarbonate roof covering a parking space and died. A single-row scaffold had been erected near and below the eaves of the second-floor roof, but the height from the edge of the second-floor roof to the handrail of the single-row scaffold was 0.5 m, and there was a gap of 0.18 m.

The victim, who was engaged in lowering carts loaded with cargo (cardboard boxes containing bottles of sake) from the second floor to the first floor using a goods elevator installed in a factory, fell 6.2 m from the second-floor elevator entrance onto the car floor on the first floor and died at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

In the process of manufacturing a steel frame for an industrial machine (223 cm wide, 250 cm deep, 89 cm high, weighing about 3.5 t), to do preparatory work before painting, the four corners of the steel frame were set on triangular-pyramid supports (62 cm high), and the victim went underneath to work when the steel frame fell off the supports and crushed the victim.

Worker B of a primary subcontractor, standing on H-beam 1, moved H-beam 1 to adjust the positions of H-beam 2 and H-beam 1 with a lever block. H-beam 4, which was assembled together with H-beam 1, moved so far that it came off the bracket supporting it, so it fell, and at the same time H-beam 1 fell, and H-beam 3, which was assembled together with H-beam 1, also fell. At that time, victim A of a secondary subcontractor, who was installing H-beam 23 on H-beam 5, was struck by the falling H-beam 1 and pinned under it.

The victim was using a forklift to unload flexible container bags stacked in two tiers from a trailer container on the slope of an unloading area. During the work, the two-tier flexible container bags became unstable, and when the victim tried to check them, the forklift started moving and the situation became dangerous, so the victim jumped down below the slope, whereupon the forklift rolled over off the slope and the victim was pinned under it.

During reinforcement work on stone masonry on a slope along a railway line, two workers were using shovels to level the soil around piles (H-beams) driven as the foundation of a leaning-type retaining wall when the stone masonry on the slope collapsed, and one worker was completely buried in soil and died.
While driving a large truck on an expressway to transport cargo, the victim crashed into the side wall at a tunnel entrance and died.

Five workers were removing small trees growing on a slope outside a golf course. The north side of the slope was the course, and the south side was a cliff. When a tree was felled with a chainsaw, it got caught on vines, so they planned to attach a rope to it and lower it to the ground. For that purpose, the victim was moving down the slope when a sound like a tree falling was heard and the victim called out "It's falling," but afterward the victim could no longer be seen, and was found at the bottom of the cliff about 40 m below.

The driver of a wing-body truck with a maximum load capacity of 3 t had stopped the truck with the gear in first, the parking brake applied, and the engine off. With one wing still raised, the driver reached in with the left arm from the road and turned the truck's ignition key with the left hand, whereupon the truck started moving; the truck's door hit the factory gate and the driver's arm was caught in the door, and the truck continued moving forward, compressing the driver's chest, and the driver died of cardiac rupture.
While delivering newspapers on a moped, the victim fell on a curve about 6 m wide and injured the head, and died about an hour and a half later at the hospital to which the victim was taken.

To assemble the steel frame of a building, the victim was about to retighten bolts on a steel beam (beam width 35 cm, about 7.4 m above the ground) when the victim fell to the ground and died of severe head trauma.
The victim climbed a standing tree and, after cutting branches with a chainsaw, fell to the ground from a height of about 5 m.
The victim was found collapsed in a corridor and taken to hospital by ambulance, but died at the hospital. The cause of death was "acute subdural hematoma."

The victim was engaged in shakeout work on sand molds for castings at the business site. The victim was found by a coworker with the left arm caught in the pulley section of a belt conveyor (installed in an underground pit) carrying sand discharged from a shakeout machine that crushes the sand of the sand molds after shakeout.

At a demolition work site, while demolishing a concrete block wall (6 blocks high by 35 blocks wide) with an engine cutter, the victim was making cuts from the left and right at the level between the first and second blocks from the bottom when the partially cut block wall (5 blocks high by 26 blocks wide) collapsed toward the victim, pinning the victim underneath. The victim was taken by ambulance but died.

At the business site's materials yard, the victim and a coworker were loading cargo onto a truck (maximum load capacity 1.35 t) when the victim fell from the truck berth and struck the head on the asphalt ground 61 cm below.

After finishing security guard duty at a construction site and changing out of uniform, the victim guided one construction vehicle and was then run over from behind by a following car belonging to a third party.

To apply a base coat before painting a steel frame (3320 mm x 3000 mm x 911 mm, weighing 1833.7 kg; hereafter "the load"), the load had been lifted with an overhead crane (2.8 t) and water that had accumulated inside the steel frame was being drained. A single sling belt was folded over and slung at one point on the load, and the load was suspended while water was drained for 2 to 3 minutes, when the sling belt suddenly broke and the load fell, pinning the victim, who was working near the load, underneath.

When someone opened a service entrance door from the inside, they found the victim lying collapsed on the road. From security camera footage, it is thought that after closing an umbrella in front of the door, the victim lost balance when turning toward the door, fell from a spot with a step, and struck the head.
While removing ceiling materials of a building from a full-deck (shelf) scaffold, the victim fell about 5 m through an opening (about 1.8 m x about 1.8 m) in the work platform and struck the floor.

To climb onto the roof of a two-story office building to work, while fixing a ladder near the roof, the ladder's lock came off and the ladder retracted and fell over, and the victim fell from a height close to the roof (about 6 m).

In a forest, Japanese bigleaf magnolia (honoki) trees were being felled to harvest logs for shiitake mushroom cultivation and to build a work road. The victim, working alone with a chainsaw, had made the undercut in a magnolia tree and was making the back cut when the trunk split lengthwise and the tree fell in an unintended direction. When a coworker working a short distance away found the victim, the victim's legs were caught under the fallen magnolia tree.

The victim was riding a small motorbike (moped) and delivering newspapers. On reaching an intersection on a national highway (a signalized intersection with good visibility), the moped and a passenger car collided at the crossing, and the victim, who was riding the moped, later died.

The victim was removing material clogging the inside of a cutter compactor at the business site. Another worker, not aware that the victim was working, pressed the start button of the cutter compactor. The victim's head and face were caught in the cutter of the cutter compactor. The victim suffered injuries to the head and face and was taken to hospital, where the victim's death was confirmed.

At the building of a waste treatment facility where the victim worked, the victim was on top of a cardboard compactor (hereafter "the compactor") assisting with the work of loading used cardboard into the compactor's feed hopper with a forklift, and was later found by a coworker lying collapsed on the work floor below the compactor. The victim was hospitalized for treatment but died.

During the felling of obstructing trees at a house, when the fourth standing tree was felled, the falling tree hit a tree that had been felled earlier and left in place, and the tree that sprang up struck the victim in the abdomen.

This accident occurred at a machine in a factory called a "heat set," which is used to heat-treat thermoplastic fibers to fix their shape and dimensions. Needle sheets called "pin sheets" are attached at regular intervals to the heat set's conveyor. At the time of the accident, a pin sheet pierced the hem of the victim's work clothes (trousers), the victim's leg was dragged by the conveyor and caught between it and a guide roll, and the victim's leg continued to be cut by the pin sheets; the victim died from massive blood loss.

While traveling in a light vehicle on an expressway to the site of new construction work on an existing facility, the victim crashed from behind into a large truck stopped ahead and died of high-energy trauma.

A fishing boat (4.6 t) left port and did not return. A fishing boat that was searching rescued three male crew members at sea about 1.2 km west of the fishing port, but their deaths were confirmed. The victims were wearing life jackets. One male crew member who had been missing was found washed ashore on a coast about 8.3 km from the place where the boat had sunk.

A fishing boat (4.6 t) left port and did not return. A fishing boat that was searching rescued three male crew members at sea about 1.2 km west of the fishing port, but their deaths were confirmed. The victims were wearing life jackets. One male crew member who had been missing was found washed ashore on a coast about 8.3 km from the place where the boat had sunk.

At a scallop processing plant, the victim, a dispatched worker, had finished shucking scallops and was walking on stairs in the plant when the victim fell and struck the forehead on the floor. At the time of the accident, the victim was conscious and walking unaided, so the victim went home once, then that night went to hospital accompanied by a person in charge from the dispatching agency and was admitted, but the victim's condition worsened and the victim died.

The wire rope of a sand discharge pipe moored (secured with wire ropes) on the harbor side of a breakwater broke, and the sand discharge pipe bulged out toward the navigation channel, with a risk of drifting into the channel. While two workers on the breakwater and ten on a work vessel were mooring the sand discharge pipe to the breakwater again, a wave overtopping the breakwater caused one worker on the breakwater to fall into the sea, and the worker died.

At a site for new construction of a garage, the victim was painting, alone, a steel frame that had been assembled up to the roof section (3.4 m high). When the representative of the client for the work visited the site, the victim was found lying on the side, bleeding, with the left side of the face on the asphalt ground inside the garage under construction. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance but died at the hospital.
During roof repair work on a two-story wooden house, the victim climbed onto the roof to install anchorage equipment for fall arrest devices and fell 7.4 m from the edge of the roof.

On the day of the accident, a coworker of the victim used a communication device (intercom) to signal the victim and others that a trial run of the conveyor operation was starting, and the trial run began. Afterward, the victim was found caught in the conveyor. At the time of the accident, the victim was near the belt conveyor.

Intending to swap a 3 t truck parked in front of the office with a 2 t truck parked at a materials yard 50 m from the office, the victim drove the 3 t truck to the materials yard and parked it, then switched to the 2 t truck. While driving within the materials yard, the 3 t truck began to roll backward toward a container in the yard, so the victim got out of the truck he was driving and stepped into the path of the 3 t truck to stop it, but it did not stop, and his body was caught between the rear of the truck and the container.
While a flexible container was being lifted and carried using a forklift, the forklift overturned, and the worker operating the machine was pinned under the forklift.

A person who normally worked in an office job and did not perform field work was doing on-site work to carry out concrete placing in place of a worker. When the victim did not return to the office, a search of the plant was made, and the victim was found buried in sand in a hopper where sand and earth/stone were stored, and death was confirmed.

At a barn attached to the premises of a private residence, while the victim was re-roofing to reinforce the slate roof of the barn while on the slate roof, without measures to prevent stepping through, the victim stepped through the slate roof. The victim fell about 4 m onto the concrete floor below and died.
While leveling the bottom of an excavated trench at a sewer pipe installation construction site, the ground collapsed and the victim was buried alive.

At the end of cleaning work on a railway car, the victim lost balance and fell while descending from the crew compartment using the handrail and footstep. The victim lost consciousness immediately after the accident and soon recovered to the point of being able to converse, but after emergency transport, cerebral contusion and subarachnoid hemorrhage were found and the victim was diagnosed as requiring inpatient treatment. The victim remained hospitalized thereafter, developed symptomatic epilepsy and pneumonia as complications of the cerebral contusion, and died of pneumonia.

To moor a floating crane, a spud (a pile driven into the seabed to anchor the vessel) was lifted with the crane, and when an attempt was made to pull out the spud's securing pin, the securing pin struck the victim.

A male customer who came into the store walked around inside and then stabbed a male clerk at the counter with a bladed weapon. When the victim and a female clerk (who had come from another store to help) who were in the backyard noticed something was wrong and returned to the store floor, the female clerk was stabbed near the center of the store, and the victim was also slashed in the backyard. According to the forensic autopsy, the victim died of hemorrhagic shock.

On a manju (steamed bun) production line, a (metal) mesh used to carry manju laid on top of it fell together with the manju between the discharge unit at the outlet of a vertical cooler (a machine for cooling steamed manju) and the belt conveyor. When the victim reached an arm into the discharge unit to remove the fallen manju, the discharge unit started operating, and the victim was caught from the arm up to the upper body.

The victim, working alone, was engaged in cutting hay rolls into small pieces with a cutting machine for mixing into compost. While the company representative was transporting cut hay that had accumulated in the compost yard with a wheel loader, he saw the victim at the feed opening inside the cutting machine and, thinking the victim was doing something dangerous, walked toward the victim. On the way, he heard the victim shout to stop the machine and stopped the cutting machine, but both of the victim's legs were severed by the cutting machine, and the victim died.

On the day of the accident, the victim was driving a garbage packer truck (automatic transmission) alone, stopped it on the road near the accident site, and got out to walk to a garbage collection box 7 to 8 m away, when the unoccupied packer truck began to move forward. The victim opened the driver's door to try to stop it, but the right front wheel dropped into a roadside ditch, the door struck the wall of a private house and closed, and the victim's head and other parts were caught between the door and the vehicle body at the driver's entrance.

While the victim was driving alone transporting steel sheets for automobiles from the workplace, upon turning left to the west at an intersection, steel sheets at the front of the cargo bed, which had been tied in bundles of 200 sheets and stacked two high, collapsed and fell, and about 180 sheets were scattered over the crosswalk. The victim pulled the trailer over to the left side beyond the intersection, turned on the hazard lights, got out, and while picking up the steel sheets on the crosswalk, was run over by a passenger car coming from the east.

When the victim did not return for some time after a break, a search of the premises was made, and the victim was found lying unconscious in a roadside ditch on the premises. The victim was taken by ambulance to a hospital, where death from hypothermia was confirmed. It was raining that day, and water had accumulated in the ditch.
The victim fell into the sea together with a company vehicle from the parking lot in front of the freezer at a general branch office, and died.

While removing concrete that had hardened inside a concrete feeding machine, the victim was working without taking measures such as turning off the power. As a result, when the hardened concrete was removed, the mixing screw in the machine began to rotate, and the victim's lower body was caught, and the victim died.

The victim was engaged in long-distance operation of a large truck on a route of loading, then unloading, then returning to the home workplace. While driving on an expressway from the unloading point back to the home workplace, the victim rear-ended a trailer dump truck that was stopped in the travel lane of the expressway main line. The victim's death was confirmed at the hospital to which he was transported.

To feed raw material into a hopper, the victim lifted a flexible container filled with raw material (weight about 760 kg) with a telpher (rated load 1 t), and while another worker was opening the discharge port at the bottom of the flexible container, a belt part of the flexible container broke, the load fell, and it struck the victim's head directly.

At a demolition site for a wooden (partly steel-frame) building, three workers preparing to carry out demolished materials were pinned under the roof and floor of the second-floor portion of the building under demolition, which collapsed; one died and two suffered minor injuries. The roof collapsed when the first-floor exterior wall in front of it was pulled down with a demolition grapple. There was snow on the roof estimated by eye at about 40 cm.
While installing toe boards on the 7th level of an external scaffold 12.8 m high, the victim fell from the side opposite the building structure.

The victim reported to the workplace at around [time not given in the original], and then went by 3 t truck to the logistics center of the consignee. While doing cargo-handling work onto the truck bed at the consignee, the victim died of acute ischemic heart failure.

To level the paved surface on the premises of a logistics warehouse, the victim was cutting a raised road surface using a small cutting (milling) machine. When the victim moved backward together with the cutting machine while operating its lever, the victim was caught between the cutting machine and a platform and died.

While resting at a parking area, because the rear camera was dirty, the victim opened the rear left door to wipe off the camera and climbed onto the upper part of the cargo body, slipped, fell from a point 1.86 m above the ground, struck the left side of the head hard on the road surface, and died of cerebral contusion.
While traveling from a business-trip destination workplace, the victim jumped down from the edge of the road, landed on a railing, and died of multiple trauma.

At a construction site for repaving an asphalt-paved road (total about 600 m), after removal of the asphalt and delivery of base course material, the victim was operating a 4 t combined roller (a compaction machine with an overall width of about 1.4 m) and compacting a road about 4.5 m wide, when the roller fell from the road shoulder into a rice-paddy irrigation channel. The victim was pinned under the combined roller and died of hemorrhagic shock due to multiple trauma.

The victim set out alone from the office driving a feed transport vehicle with a maximum load capacity of 7.3 t. After loading cattle feed and while heading to a ranch, the vehicle broke through a guardrail on a prefectural road and fell about 5 m.

At a silicon single-crystal pulling machine (Unit No. 390), after the upper two chambers of a tank-shaped three-part chamber (body section; it had contained argon gas) were opened, Victim A crouched down inside the lower bottom chamber (depth 80 cm, outer diameter 158 cm) to remove electrode parts at the bottom and clean off dirt, lost consciousness, and died at a later date.

In a food supermarket under renovation, while the victim was unpacking a refrigerated (freezer) showcase (width 1568 x height 1940 x depth 900 mm, mass 280 kg) on a dolly that had been brought in for installation, including removing protective tape and unneeded posted materials, the showcase fell over and the victim was pinned under it. The victim was taken by ambulance and died.

When the victim was loading a hydraulic excavator with a machine weight of 0.75 t onto a dump truck with a maximum load capacity of 3.8 t, using two ramp boards (about 3 m long and about 0.45 m wide) placed against the truck bed, the ramp boards came off the dump truck bed, and at the same time the hydraulic excavator and the victim operating it fell to the ground. The victim was pinned under the hydraulic excavator and died.

At a revetment construction site, in order to build a work access road for use in removing sheet piles installed to prevent river water from flowing into the work area, the victim tried to descend a sloped revetment with an excavator (backhoe). The excavator tilted and overturned to the left, the victim was thrown from the operator's seat and pinned under the overturned excavator, and died instantly of chest crush injury.

At a plant, the victim was found collapsed inside an underground pit (a cylindrical tank about 160 cm in diameter and about 160 cm high) in a chemical products tank yard. The victim was then taken to a hospital but died. The victim had been draining water from a crude light oil tank; when the victim did not return even near the end of working hours, others sensed something was wrong, searched, and found the victim in the pit.

On the roof of a warehouse, the victim was cutting branches overhanging from the slope beside the warehouse. The warehouse roof was covered with slate; the victim stepped through it, fell about 3.5 m onto the concrete floor below, and died.

The victim was engaged in diving work, cleaning the inside of a water tank at the accident site at a water depth of about 7 m. About one hour after work began, the communication attendant waiting at the top of the tank could no longer hear the victim's breathing sounds (via underwater telephone). The fire department carried out a rescue, and the victim was found underwater with the mask detached.

The victim was working alone stacking dies whose production had ended two high in the die storage area. The die was rigged with four belt slings, but when the crane lifting operation was performed with one sling inadvertently left unattached, the die, now hanging from a single sling, shifted, and the victim, who was operating the crane, was caught between dies and crushed to death.

At a construction site for a new regional high-standard road, while the victim was operating a vibratory roller compacting embankment fill, the victim fell together with the roller about 1.5 m from the road shoulder. The fallen roller was upside down, and the victim was found lying beside it. The victim was taken to a hospital but died of hemorrhagic shock.

Inside the shipper's plant, bundles of the product, steel sheets for formwork (deck plates with rebar trusses, about 5 m long), were being loaded 3 rows by 3 tiers onto a 10 t truck driven by the victim. While the shipper's forklift (hereinafter FL; [the on-site subcontracted loading/unloading operator] was adjusting the position of a top-tier bundle), the victim, on the cargo bed on the opposite side, was securing the load using a chain lever, when the top-tier bundle (about 400 kg) was pushed out by the FL and fell, striking the victim; they both fell to the ground and the victim was pinned under it.

During demolition work on an existing building with an atrium opening between the first and second floors, the victim used a demolition grapple (machine weight 1.68 t) to grip the lifting loop of a flexible container bag (estimated weight 100 kg) containing second-floor interior demolition material (tile carpet) and swung to the left, whereupon the demolition grapple lost balance. The victim was thrown from the machine, fell about 3.6 m to the first-floor surface below, and was pinned under the demolition grapple, which fell after him.

At a road repair construction site, the victim entered an excavated area to correct the tilt of steel plates set up there to prevent collapse of the slope face and scouring of the slope face by spring water, whereupon the slope face collapsed and the victim was buried under the falling earth and sand.

On the premises of the workplace, a tree broken by heavy snow had become lodged in another tree, and its tip was blocking a passageway, so it was decided to remove the lodged tree. It is presumed that the victim climbed a ladder leaning against the lodged tree and, while cutting the lodged tree with a chainsaw, fell from the ladder to the ground. The victim was taken to a hospital but died.

During renovation of the inspection walkway of an overhead traveling crane (17 t), the victim was using an aerial work platform to measure the dimensions of a steel plate (144 cm x 54 cm) on the underside of the walkway at a height of about 7 m, and fell from the gate section of the aerial work platform's work deck.

At a river maintenance construction site, during felling of a standing tree (about 15 m tall, diameter at breast height about 49 cm), the victim used a chainsaw to make the face notch and then the back cut, whereupon the tree split vertically upward from the back cut, and the lower end of the split portion struck the victim's chest. The victim was taken to a medical facility but died the same day of severe chest trauma.

While the victim was driving a turret-type in-plant transport vehicle (hereinafter "turret truck"), the victim was thrown from the turret truck to the ground for some reason, struck the chest hard from the impact, and died.
A single-vehicle traffic accident occurred while the victim was delivering (relocating) a rental car. (The vehicle crashed into the guardrail on the left side of the road.)

As deputy section manager of the General Affairs Team, General Affairs Section, engaged in restoration of electric power facilities following an earthquake, the victim was in charge of rear support for power restoration work and of filing applications with government authorities concerning labor matters, such as applications under Article 33 of the Labor Standards Act, and developed subarachnoid hemorrhage.

The victim carried test weights used for elevator inspection (40 kg: two 20 kg weights) in both hands several times, after which blurred vision in the left eye and headache developed, and the victim visited a hospital. The diagnosis was migraine. At home, when lifting a 1.2 kg load, the victim lost vision in the left eye and the right side of the body became paralyzed, and the victim was taken by ambulance and hospitalized. At the hospital the victim developed cerebral infarction; emergency thrombectomy was performed, but impaired consciousness continued, and the victim died.

In a plant, while machining a metal part on an engine lathe, the victim was pressing sandpaper with both hands against the rotating workpiece to finish its surface, when the cotton work glove worn on the left hand was caught by the rotating workpiece, and the momentum caused the victim's head to strike the chuck of the lathe, and the victim died.

At a construction site for replacing a corrugated galvanized iron roof, the victim, who was removing, carrying, and stacking the existing corrugated iron roofing, stepped onto an existing wood wool board to carry removed corrugated iron to the stacking area, stepped through the wood wool board, and fell 8.27 m onto the concrete floor below.

To pump out human waste from a private house, a sanitation truck (vacuum truck) was parked on the road and two people were working. The victim noticed the sanitation truck slowly rolling backward and tried to stop it by hand, was caught between the private house's concrete block wall and the sanitation truck, and died. The road where the sanitation truck was parked had a slope of 2 degrees.
As a business-trip assignment, while pruning a pine tree, a branch of the pine tree being used as footing broke, and the victim fell from a height of about 5.6 m and struck the head on the ground.

The victim was unloading sugarcane using a dump truck with a crane (maximum load capacity 6.6 t). Because sugarcane remained on the truck bed, the victim instructed the driver to tilt the bed and went around to the rear of the bed, whereupon the rear gate of the bed, which had been opened out to the side of the vehicle body, closed under its own weight, and the victim was caught between the rear of the dump truck and the rear gate, and died.
At a delivery destination's premises, the driver, who was doing cargo-handling work on the bed of a truck (flatbed / 8 t), fell from the bed and suffered a head injury.
A vessel operated by the victim that had left port (gross tonnage 1.1 t, one person aboard) collided with a vessel sailing to enter port (gross tonnage 9.7 t, one person aboard).

The victim left home saying he was going to the plant on a day off, and when he had not returned by night, the victim's family, finding this suspicious, telephoned the plant manager. The plant manager searched the plant and found the victim unconscious inside a cleaning tank used for degreasing with trichloroethylene.

While doing pile extraction work, the victim, together with coworker A, entered an area excavated with an excavator (backhoe) and was digging the ground by hand with a shovel to check the pile head, when the slope face collapsed and the victim's lower body was buried in earth and sand. The victim was conscious when rescued from the earth and sand, but death was confirmed at the hospital to which the victim was transported.

In a warehouse on the workplace premises, while moving a rack about 3.5 m high, the victim stood on top of a pallet tied with a cord to the top of the rack and tried to cut the cord, lost balance, fell together with the pallet, struck the middle tier of the rack, and then fell onto the concrete floor. After the accident, the victim was hospitalized with a cervical spine injury, subsequently developed acute renal failure as a complication, and died.

During felling of a pine tree damaged by pine wilt disease (tree height 31 m, diameter at breast height 43 cm), the victim was pulling the tree with a Tirfor (wire rope hoist) to adjust the felling direction while the feller was cutting the back cut with a chainsaw. The tree fell about 90 degrees off from the originally planned northward direction, toward the east, and struck the victim, who was holding down the Tirfor.

While delivering newspapers, as the victim walked down a slope on foot, the road was frozen, and the victim slipped and fell on the asphalt road surface, striking the back of the head on the ground. The victim later died of acute subdural hematoma.

The victim and one other person were transporting large sandbags using a vehicle-type construction machine (1.3 t mobile crane specification) to restore a collapsed slope of a rice paddy, when the vehicle-type construction machine driven by the victim rolled over from the top of the slope toward the rice paddy, and the victim was caught between the ground surface and the machine and died.

To cut down a bamboo thicket and level the ground on private land, the victim was crossing a bridge over a residential road (with no safety features such as railings or load limit signs; builder and administrator unknown) with a small excavator (backhoe) (vehicle weight about 1.7 t), when the center portion of the bridge could not bear the weight and collapsed. The victim fell together with the excavator about 3.9 m into the stream below, was pinned under the excavator, and died.

While the victim was driving himself from the workplace to a facility at a business-trip destination, he developed subarachnoid hemorrhage, crossed into the opposite lane, and collided with a large trailer. The victim was then taken by ambulance to a hospital, where death was confirmed.

During work to transfer steel materials that had been transported by ship onto a 30 t trailer using a mobile crane, after the slung steel materials were lowered onto the trailer bed, the victim tried to remove the slinging gear, lost footing, and fell from the 2.3 m-high work position to the ground. The victim was taken to a hospital in critical condition, unconscious, but later died.

The victim was found lying on top of the ceiling of the car of an elevator (posted load capacity 240 kg) installed in the workplace. When the victim was found, the elevator car was stopped at the first floor, the first-floor hoistway door was fully open, and the third-floor hoistway door was open about 30 cm.

The victim, a dispatched worker, was engaged in repacking automobile parts in a warehouse of the client workplace. After symptoms such as hand spasms were observed in the break room, the victim went outside, suddenly started running, and fell. The victim was foaming at the mouth and snoring and was taken by ambulance, but died of heatstroke.

The victim left the head office sales office by truck that day and, after loading cargo at this workplace's logistics warehouse and several other workplaces, was driving on a national highway (outbound lane) toward the shipper's destination, when he rear-ended another truck waiting at a traffic signal at an intersection. As a result, the victim died of multiple trauma to the whole body.
While driving back from a site to the branch office, the victim had a single-vehicle accident, colliding with the guardrail of the median strip, and died.

The victim was engaged in repairing cracks in the walls and floor of an eel farming tank (tank depth 1.4 m). A worker other than the victim who came to the work location found the victim collapsed, and at that time a movable ladder used for going up and down was lying fallen beside the victim. Other workers had heard a metallic crashing sound.
