After loading cargo onto the bed of a large truck (low-floor flatbed, maximum load capacity 14.3 t), the victim, alone, was putting a cover sheet over the load while standing on the load, when the victim fell from the first tier of flexible container bags (round type for 1 t, actual weight about 500 kg) stacked two high, and struck the head hard on the asphalt surface about 2.5 m below (presumed). One of the rubber boots the victim had been wearing was left on top of the first tier of flexible container bags. The victim was not wearing a safety helmet or safety belt.

The victim was surveying the current use of farmland alone. Because the company received no notice that the survey was finished, coworkers searched and found the victim pinned under a car on a sloped road.

At a water main installation construction site, the victim was guiding a 4 t dump truck that was backing up an uphill road (maximum slope about 17 degrees) to the construction site, when the 4 t dump truck suddenly moved backward and the victim was caught between the rear of the truck bed and a wall at the side of the road.

The victim and a coworker rode in a light (kei) truck to pick up a company-owned 10 t truck at a port. On the way back to the company, with the coworker driving the 10 t truck and the victim driving the light truck, on a national highway bypass, the light truck driven by the victim crossed the center line and collided head-on with a medium-size truck in the oncoming lane.

During roadside ditch cleaning work, after cleaning a catch basin at the edge of the road, the victim was about to install a net inside the basin to prevent leaves and other debris from flowing out. To attach it at a net depth of 1 m, the victim was lying face-down on the road reaching in with the hands, when a nearby high-pressure washing truck moved forward and its front wheel ran over the worker's abdomen. The victim was taken by ambulance and was undergoing treatment but later died.

Two trucks were stopped in a truck berth. When the driver of truck A started the truck, the driver of truck B was also about to start, so truck A was backed up to let truck B go first, whereupon the victim (a dispatched worker), who was behind the truck, was struck by the truck. The victim's abdomen was severely caught between the truck and the platform; the victim was taken to a hospital, where death was confirmed.

A chain-reaction collision involving an express bus (hereinafter "bus") and three trucks. The truck driven by the victim was traveling at the very rear and rear-ended the bus ahead, which was nearly stopped.

There is equipment that feeds plastic crushed by a crusher through piping into a tank about 4 m high. Because a blockage occurred at a pipe flange connecting to the tank at a height of about 4 m, four pallets were placed on the forks of a forklift, and the victim stood on them, using the forklift for a purpose other than its intended use, to remove the blockage. To remove the blockage, the victim moved from the pallets on the forklift onto the top of the tank about 4 m high, and while returning to the pallets, accidentally fell.

In snow removal and hauling work, the victim was serving as a guide for snow-hauling dump trucks at a snow dumping site. As a dump truck entered, the victim was moving behind a parked snow removal dozer to guide it, when the snow removal dozer backed up. At that time the victim fell, and the victim's head was run over by the right rear tire of the backing snow removal dozer, and the victim died.

At a demolition site, waste materials were being loaded onto a dump truck using a demolition grapple. In this work, the victim was engaged in leveling the waste materials on the dump truck bed and load. At this time, the victim was found sitting on the ground, unconscious.

During a patrol inspection including lighting tests and bulb replacement, the victim was found collapsed inside an elevator and taken by ambulance, and died. Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, cerebral contusion, subdural hematoma, and rib fractures. According to the building's security camera footage, the victim fell from a stepladder (height 1.4 m) while replacing a ceiling bulb. After a while the victim got up and continued working, but was later seen standing in a dazed state inside the elevator and then collapsed.
The victim, who was doing finishing work inside a cargo tank of a chemical tanker under construction, fell for some reason about 12 m to the tank bottom.

On an expanded polystyrene injection molding machine, the victim, who was working inside the molding machine taking out molded products and attaching metal fittings for the next product to the mold, had the head caught in the mold and died. No helmet was worn. The molding machine was installed on a stand, the victim entered the inside of the machine from below the stand to work, and at the time of the accident the machine was running in fully automatic operation. The safety door on the side of the machine was open, and the door interlock had been disabled.

In bridge repair work, while using a steel pry bar and other tools to remove a tree stump (about 45 cm) that was obstructing formwork installation, the victim fell from the foot of the bridge, at a height of about 4 m, to the riverbed and died.

While the victim was skidding and yarding felled trees using a grapple, the victim, for some reason, was caught between the cylinder of the grapple's boom and the frame of the cab. The right side window glass of the cab of the grapple the victim was operating was broken.

To cut and remove a gas branch pipe running from a gas main to a house, the victim began digging a hole about 50 cm long, about 40 cm wide, and about 80 cm deep with a shovel. A coworker doing the same kind of work about 30 m away checked the location and found the victim unconscious with the head in the excavated hole. The victim was taken by ambulance, but death was confirmed the same day. The inner diameter of the gas branch pipe was 3 cm, and at the time of discovery about 50 cm of it had been removed.

The victim, as captain of a work boat (gross tonnage under 5 t, capacity 5 persons, with outboard motor) chartered to a construction consulting company, carried two persons from that company out to sea from a pier near a fishing port. After navigating the designated waters for surveying, as the boat approached the lake mouth to return to the pier, it was hit by a wave from behind and capsized. The victim and one passenger drifted about 100 m offshore and were rescued, but died.

The victim, with one coworker, boarded a chartered work boat with a captain (gross tonnage under 5 t, capacity 5 persons, with outboard motor), went out to sea from a pier near a fishing port, and carried out seabed surveying near the lake mouth. After finishing the work, as the boat approached the lake mouth to return to the pier in the lake, it was hit by a wave from behind and capsized. The coworker made it to shore on his own, but the victim and the captain drifted about 100 m offshore and were rescued, but died.

In clear-cutting work in a privately owned forest, work was being done by a method in which a coworker gripped and piled up cedars felled by the victim with a chainsaw using a timber grapple machine. The operator of the timber grapple machine became suspicious that the next felling was not taking place, checked on the victim, and found the victim collapsed near a stump. Near where the victim was found, a felled tree was lying overhead, and collapsed rocks were observed.

While unlocking the closure ropes installed at eight entrances to a park's waterside facilities, the victim fell or otherwise struck the head hard on stone steps in the park. The victim died of cerebral contusion with acute subdural hematoma at the hospital where the victim was admitted.

While three workers employed by the same company were traveling to a site in a company vehicle (light wagon), the vehicle collided with a roadside tree on a national highway. The three were taken to a hospital; the passenger in the front passenger seat suffered a severe blow to the chest, and death from chest trauma was confirmed at the hospital. The driver suffered a cervical spine fracture, and the passenger behind the front passenger seat suffered serious injuries including spinal cord injury. The accident site was a straight road with one lane in each direction and good visibility, and the road surface was frozen at the time of the accident.
While delivering morning newspapers by motorcycle, the victim collided at an intersection with a truck traveling east through a red light.

In the company's own parking lot, during the pre-departure inspection of the ready-mixed concrete mixer truck the victim drove for deliveries, while inspecting around the engine the victim heard the sound of an object falling under the shaft that rotates the drum, and, without stopping the engine, put the right hand in from the side of the rubber shaft cover (intended to prevent oil splatter) to pick it up, whereupon the sleeve of the work clothes was caught by the shaft. The victim was taken to a hospital and, while under treatment for amputation of the right upper arm, died of sepsis.

While parts were being replaced on a multi-level parking structure (4 levels) attached to an apartment building, the victim was crossing over pallets on which automobiles are loaded on the 4th level of the parking structure to move to the work location. Another worker noticed an abnormal noise and checked the source, and the victim, who had been moving on the 4th-level pallets, was found collapsed on the 1st level.

During installation of an evacuation hatch on the balcony side of an apartment building, while the victim was using a stepladder on a third-floor balcony to install laundry-drying hardware and do other work, the victim went over the balcony railing and fell from a height of about 7 m onto an outdoor asphalt-paved parking lot.

During steel erection for construction of a new plant, a steel column fitted with girts was lifted with a rough terrain crane, and the victim, in order to bolt it to a beam, climbed onto the steel frame using the wedge-connection-type scaffold around the steel frame and the steel angles, and walked on the 17.5 cm-wide beam or the 10 cm-wide girt beside the beam toward the bolting position, when the victim fell 5.8 m to the ground below.

The victim was struck by the bucket of an excavator (backhoe) and died. That day, rubble was being removed from a basement through an opening created after a boiler was dismantled. The victim was a dump truck driver and had no need to enter the basement, but entered it for some reason, came within the working range of the excavator being used to remove the rubble, and was struck by the bucket. The victim lost consciousness immediately after the accident and later died.

The victim, who was working alone using an excavator (backhoe) to sort concrete debris from excavated surplus soil, was found lying on his back, unconscious and bleeding from the left ear, on concrete debris beside the excavator. The victim was then taken to a hospital, where death was confirmed.
While the victim was driving a mixer truck toward a construction site, the truck went over the median strip, overturned, and collided with a truck traveling in the opposite lane.

During a break, after finishing a meal, the victim was riding a bicycle along a U passage within the workplace when he was struck from behind by a private car being driven by a worker of an on-site subcontractor who was leaving work. The victim's head struck the car's windshield hard, and he then fell to the ground. The victim was taken by ambulance to a hospital the same day but died.

In a plant, the victim was found lying face-down on the floor near the conveyor control panel of an NC plasma cutting machine for cutting steel plates, and death was confirmed the same day at the hospital to which the victim was transported.

During assembly of a tube-and-clamp scaffold around the building structure for exterior wall renovation of a four-story reinforced concrete building, the victim was found lying face-down on the ground bleeding from the head, and later died.

While riding in the basket of an aerial work platform and painting the underside of an overhanging deck about 5 m above the floor of a 9000 t press, the victim's head was caught between that part and the basket's handrail.

Inside a stainless steel container for used gravure ink (113 cm long x 113 cm wide x 145 cm high, capacity 1050 L), the victim was scraping off ink adhering to the inside of the container with a scraper and then performing cleaning work such as pouring in ethyl acetate and scrubbing with a wire scrubber, when the victim lost consciousness. The victim was not wearing an air-line mask or similar respiratory protection.
In a yard, while sugarcane was being transported by a tractor shovel, the victim was caught by the vehicle as it moved backward.

The accident became known when a golf course customer contacted the workplace reception to report that someone was lying on the ground. On a side path of the golf course, which was the accident site, a vehicle used for bunker maintenance was found overturned on its right side, and the victim was found lying on his back near the vehicle. The victim was taken to a hospital and underwent surgery, but death was confirmed.

On the bed of a 10 t truck about 3 m above the ground, while the victim was loading rice in a flexible container bag lifted by another worker with a forklift onto the truck bed, the victim lost balance, fell to the ground, and died.

While loading cardboard into a packer (garbage) truck, the (unoccupied) vehicle ran away, and when the victim tried to stop it, the victim was run over by the vehicle. The packer truck's parking position was on a slope; the transmission was in neutral and the parking brake was applied, but wheel chocks were not used.

In an aluminum plate cutting plant, while two aluminum plates (weight 250 kg) were being lifted and moved using a 2.8 t overhead traveling crane, a fiber belt came off the crane hook, and the aluminum plates fell from a height of 2 m and struck the victim's head.

In connection with installing a stormwater conduit, the victim entered the bottom of a 1.47 m-deep excavation dug with an excavator (backhoe) to relocate an existing water pipe and was giving directions on where to excavate, when the ground behind the victim collapsed and a chunk of asphalt struck the victim.

The accident site was a former golf course, where solar panels are now installed over the entire course. The victim, guarding the solar panels at the accident site, was patrolling by car along a road that had been the golf course's cart path, when the car ran off into a roadside ditch beside the cart path. Thereafter, under some circumstances, the victim fell into a pond and died.

While returning home by bicycle after finishing the day's work, the victim was found by a passerby lying on the sidewalk and taken by ambulance, but died the same day of cardiac arrest (fatal arrhythmia).

In the workplace parking lot, while standing on a three-legged stepladder pruning a standing tree, the victim fell for some reason to the (asphalt-paved) ground. The victim was working alone. After the accident, a passerby found the victim lying on the ground, and the victim was taken by ambulance but died of traumatic cerebral hemorrhage and other injuries.
The victim was found pinned under a 1 t flexible container bag on the forks (with a pallet) of a forklift raised to a height of 3.6 m.

The victim, who was scraping off mud adhering to a roller of the discharge conveyor of a leaf-stripping facility (a facility for removing leaves and mud from sugarcane raw material) with a spatula about 20 cm long, had the left arm and head caught between the roller and the belt and died of asphyxiation. A "footing" was provided under the roller for this work, but it was narrow, had no safe walkway or handrails, and the distance between the "footing" and the roller was so small that one could not stand upright.

While the victim was wiping the upper conveyor section (height 2.5 m) of a castella (sponge cake) production line in a plant with a mop, the victim lost footing and fell. Death was confirmed at a later date. The victim was working alone at the time and was not wearing a fall arrest device or safety helmet.

While on night security duty alone at a facility, the victim was walking to activate the startup device of the mechanical security system when he fell backward and struck the back of the head on the concrete pavement. The next morning, facility staff arriving for work found the victim lying down, and the victim was taken by ambulance but died at the medical facility.

A truck driver backed the truck up to the company's own refrigerated warehouse, and while unloading cargo (refrigerated fried-chicken ingredients, etc., total weight about 200 kg) loaded on a roll box pallet, was pinned under the roll box pallet.

For blasting work by two workers, the victim was waiting at the handover location for the explosives to be used in the blasting. The victim was found lying on his back as if he had fallen out of the driver's seat of a vehicle used for transporting explosives and other purposes, with the driver's door open, the left foot inside the driver's compartment, the right foot, with its safety boot off, on the step used for getting in and out of the driver's seat, and the body from the buttocks to the head on the ground outside the vehicle.
In a privately owned forest, a worker felled a cedar about 30 m tall with a chainsaw, and the felled tree fell toward another worker (the victim) and struck him.

In the harbor of a thermal power plant, as part of harbor dredging work, a total of four people, one worker of the prime contractor and three workers of the victim's employer, were removing sand and stones from the seabed. Two workers of the victim's employer were doing diving work (scuba diving), and one worker of the prime contractor and one worker of the victim's employer were monitoring the diving work on board the boat, when one of the workers diving drowned for some reason.

The victim used a waist-belt-type fall arrest device attached via a self-retracting lifeline to the roof of the loading area, and after doing loading work and other tasks on the bed of a truck-mounted crane, got into the driver's seat alone to transport the load and started the vehicle while still wearing the fall arrest device, whereupon tension was applied to the fall arrest device and it constricted the victim's abdomen. The victim died the same day at the medical facility to which he was transported of rupture of the aorta near the liver.

After checking the control panel on top of a gantry crane girder to investigate a malfunction of a lifting magnet (a slinging device), the victim was descending a ladder way to move to the operator's cab at the bottom of the crane girder, when he fell from around the third rung from the top, and in doing so went backward over a handrail about 1.2 m high on the landing where he fell, falling about 6 m in total to the ground.

To install a boarding gangway on a launched ship, a three-dimensional gangway section, part of the boarding gangway, was installed with a jib crane with a lifting capacity of 73.7 t. Four workers were then removing four shackles at the ends of the slinging wire ropes from the lifting fittings, and when the jib crane hoisting operation was performed on signal, the shackle the victim was responsible for had not yet been removed, and the victim was caught around the neck between the slinging wire rope and the handrail of the three-dimensional gangway.

To scour yarn, a mixed solution of water, hydrogen peroxide, caustic soda, and a stabilizer heated to about 120 degrees C was used for heat treatment for 40 minutes in the dyeing tank of a high-pressure dyeing machine (Class 1 pressure vessel), after which the solution was discharged underground, and the victim, who was underground, was injured by being doused with the discharged hot solution. The victim died of septic shock at the medical facility to which he was transported.

The victim, a physician, did not immediately operate on a transported patient who required surgery, and was reproached by a fellow physician for the delay in surgery. Afterward, the victim committed suicide by jumping from a building near his home.

The victim carried clamps to the top level of a scaffold, and while approaching the work supervisor to get the next instructions, did not notice an opening provided in the scaffold stage for hoisting materials, fell 24.8 m, and died. At the time of the fall the victim was wearing a safety helmet but was not equipped with a fall arrest device.
